pullRequest.title: feat(config): insert new keys where they're documented
pullRequest.body:
This PR improves the behavior of `atuin config set` and `atuin config enable` when modifying keys that aren't in the user's `config.toml`.

The default `config.toml` we generate contains many commented-out examples of keys like this:

```toml
## enable or disable automatic sync
# auto_sync = false
```

If you run `atuin config set auto_sync true`, you might expect the new value to be written somewhere near that example. But instead, it's inserted below `enter_accept`, which is *over 140* lines away. A user might then open the file, believe the value wasn't set because they don't see it, and uncomment the example and set it themselves. This will then cause the config to *fail to deserialize* due to the duplicate keys.

When setting a key that isn't in the user's config yet, this PR searches for commented-out examples of that key, and if found, will either uncomment the example and change the value (if we believe it's safe to overwrite the comment), or insert the new key-value assignment below the example we found so it's in an expected location.

The precise logic is explained in the documentation of `enable_example` in `comment.rs`.

This PR also fixes a related issue involving the creation of tables: new tables get inserted between a different table's header and its examples, thereby invalidating that table's examples. See example 4 below for more details.

## Examples

Examples of `atuin config` before and after this PR:

### 1. Top-level key

```
atuin config set search_mode daemon-fuzzy
```

**Before:** the key is added at the end of the top-level section, over 100 lines after the comment that documents it. The commented-out example is left in-place, and if a user later uncomments it, the config will fail to deserialize.

```diff
@@ -155,4 +155,5 @@
 ## This applies for new installs. Old installs will keep the old behaviour unless configured otherwise.
 enter_accept = true
+search_mode = "daemon-fuzzy"
```

**After:** the commented-out example gets enabled and set to the new value.

```diff
@@ -29,5 +29,5 @@
 ## which search mode to use for interactive search
 ## possible values: prefix, fulltext, fuzzy, daemon-fuzzy
-# search_mode = "fuzzy"
+search_mode = "daemon-fuzzy"
```

### 2. Nested key

```
atuin config set threads.mouse true
```

**Before:** the key is inserted right under the table header, above 32 lines of unrelated comments.

```diff
 [threads]
+mouse = true
 ## Threads are your AI coding agents' sessions (Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Pi),
 ## captured by the daemon so you can search and resume them, here or on another machine.
```

**After:**

```diff
 ## list. While the picker has it, most terminals select text with shift held while dragging.
 ## Defaults to the top-level no_mouse (so on, unless that is set).
-# mouse = true
+mouse = true
```

### 3. Multiple keys at once

```
atuin config enable daemon
```

**Before:**

```diff
 enter_accept = true
+search_mode = "daemon-fuzzy"
 
@@ -252,4 +253,6 @@
 [daemon]
+enabled = true
+autostart = true
 ## Enables using the daemon to sync.
 # enabled = false
```

**After:**

```diff
 ## possible values: prefix, fulltext, fuzzy, daemon-fuzzy
-# search_mode = "fuzzy"
+search_mode = "daemon-fuzzy"
 
@@ -253,9 +253,9 @@
 [daemon]
 ## Enables using the daemon to sync.
-# enabled = false
+enabled = true
 
 ## Automatically start and manage the daemon when needed.
 ## Not compatible with `systemd_socket = true`.
-# autostart = false
+autostart = true
```

### 4. New table

```
atuin config enable output-capture
```

Creates the `[output]` table, which isn't in the default config.

**Before:** `[output]` is inserted right after `[ui]`, but *before* all of `[ui]`'s examples. If those examples were uncommented they would be incorrectly interpreted as keys in `[output]`.

```diff
@@ -252,4 +252,6 @@
 [daemon]
+enabled = true
+autostart = true
 ## Enables using the daemon to sync.
 # enabled = false
@@ -282,4 +284,5 @@
 [pty_proxy]
+enabled = true
 ## If enabled, `atuin init` will first re-exec your shell inside `atuin pty-proxy`,
 ## so you don't need a separate `eval "$(atuin pty-proxy init)"` line in your shell
@@ -392,4 +395,7 @@
 [ui]
+
+[output]
+enabled = true
 ## Columns to display in the interactive search, from left to right.
 ## The selection indicator (" > ") is always shown first implicitly.
```

**After:** `[output]` is inserted *after* `[ui]`'s comments.

```diff
@@ -253,9 +253,9 @@
 [daemon]
 ## Enables using the daemon to sync.
-# enabled = false
+enabled = true
 
 ## Automatically start and manage the daemon when needed.
 ## Not compatible with `systemd_socket = true`.
-# autostart = false
+autostart = true
 
@@ -289,5 +289,5 @@
 ## Safe to combine with an existing `atuin pty-proxy init` line — the proxy only
 ## starts once.
-# enabled = false
+enabled = true
 
 [theme]
@@ -435,2 +435,5 @@
 ## Not available on all platforms (e.g. Windows).
 # syntax_highlight = true
+
+[output]
+enabled = true
```

### 5. Preserves user-written comments

If a user has written comments that look like examples, we don't overwrite their comments, but we do use them as a guide for where to insert the key.

Assume a user has this config:

```toml
auto_sync = true

# played around with these heights, but using the default for now:
# inline_height = 100
# inline_height = 20

[sync]
records = true
```

And then runs:

```
atuin config set inline_height 50
```

**Before:** the key is inserted after the last top-level key, which could be arbitrarily far away from the commented-out examples.

```diff
 auto_sync = true
+inline_height = 50
 
 # played around with these heights, but using the default for now:
```

**After:** the key is inserted below the example comments, but without modifying them.

```diff
 # inline_height = 100
 # inline_height = 20
+inline_height = 50
```

### Description of changes

pullRequest.title: CLI option to also show closed ports
pullRequest.body:
This PR introduces the new CLI option `--closed`, which enables the option to also show ports which are closed. From a security perspective, it is very useful information to see whether we got any response at all for a given port, even when the response is a RST (conn-refused). It can indicate that our request was denied (or specifically blocked by a firewall). Currently this behavior is behind the `--closed` CLI flag and not enabled by default. Nmap, for example, shows closed ports by default. Regarding the output of the `--closed` option, it mimics the output for open ports, but instead of `Open` it shows `Closed` right before the IP Address. If the `-g` (grepable) option is set, first all open ports are printed for each IPs, then the text **_closed ports:_** is printed and the same output is repeated for all closed ports.
Here is an example:
``` .----. .-. .-. .----..---. .----. .---. .--. .-. .-. | {} }| { } |{ {__ {_ _}{ {__ / ___} / {} \ | `| | | .-. \| {_} |.-._} } | | .-._} }\ }/ /\ \| |\ | `-' `-'`-----'`----' `-' `----' `---' `-' `-'`-' `-' The Modern Day Port Scanner. ________________________________________ : http://discord.skerritt.blog : : https://github.com/RustScan/RustScan : -------------------------------------- TreadStone was here 🚀 [~] The config file is expected to be at "/********/.rustscan.toml" [~] Automatically increasing ulimit value to 50000. Closed [10.100.0.1]:22 Open [10.100.0.1]:2222 10.100.0.1 -> [2222] closed ports: 10.100.0.1 -> [22] ```
And with the -g option:
``` 10.100.0.1 -> [2222] closed ports: 10.100.0.1 -> [22] ```

pullRequest.title: Add thread name lookup tests, lookup again after 1 second if not matched at first
pullRequest.body:
- Adds the tests for #790 as requested in [this comment](https://github.com/benfred/py-spy/pull/790#issuecomment-6087480396); 
- Includes a fix that aligns with the idea in #863 which asked for a backoff on repeated thread name lookups.

The tests added cover a thread that gets its name after its first sample. Before the fix that thread would have no name until another thread starts. This happens when `threading` is imported after py-spy attaches. It also happened in 3 of 10 runs to a thread started while another thread was CPU-bound.

The fix looks the names up again when a thread without a name is sampled more than 1 second after the last lookup.

If you prefer not to change the logic and only pull the tests let me know and I will drop the retry after 1 second.

pullRequest.title: fix(regexp): enable Unicode matching for the v flag
pullRequest.body:
Closes #5571.

`/^(?:\D\b)$/iv.test("\u212a")` currently returns false. The conversion to `regress::Flags` enables Unicode-aware matching only for `u`, leaving `v` word boundaries in non-Unicode mode. Enable the backend's `unicode` flag for either JavaScript Unicode flag, while preserving the separate `unicode_sets` flag and the public `.unicode` / `.unicodeSets` getters.

The regression covers Kelvin sign and long s with `iv`, `iu`, plain `v`, and plain `i`, plus `\w`, `\W`, and the exposed flag getters. This follows [HasEitherUnicodeFlag and WordCharacters](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/text-processing.html#sec-wordcharacters).

Validation:

- The new regression fails on the original implementation at the issue's Kelvin-sign example.
- `cargo test -p boa_engine -p boa_parser --lib -j 2`: 1,452 passed, 1 ignored.
- All ten regression assertions also pass in Node.js.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Clippy passes for the affected packages with all targets, and for the entire workspace with all features/all targets and with no default features. Each run uses `-D warnings -A clippy::incompatible_msrv`: strict Clippy on this ARM Mac reports an existing MSRV diagnostic at `core/engine/src/builtins/number/conversions.rs:85` (`__jcvt`, introduced by #5577, outside this change). Toolchain: Rust 1.98.0.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and testing.

pullRequest.title: feat(studio): open a design system from a #url= or #spec= link
pullRequest.body:
Studio can now open a design system from a link, so Theme Explorer's "Open in Panda Studio" button can point straight at its hosted specs.

```
https://studio.panda-css.com/#url=<encoded https URL>&theme=<name>
https://studio.panda-css.com/#spec=gz:<base64url gzip JSON>&theme=<name>
```

Links go through the same load path as paste and drop (now shared as `openSpec`). `theme` preselects a variant and falls back to the default if it doesn't exist. Bad links show the error toast and stay on home.

Limits: https or localhost only, 10s timeout, 10 MB max, and 200k chars max for `gz:` payloads. I also widened the CSP `connect-src`, since `'self'` would block every `#url=` fetch in production.

To try it, `pnpm --filter studio spec-link` prints both link types for the sample spec.

Tested with unit tests (`utils/spec-link.test.ts`) and in Chrome against the live `panda-theme-explorer.vercel.app/specs/sketch.json`. Haven't checked the CSP on a deployed build yet, so worth a look on the preview.

pullRequest.title: fix(profiles): refresh remote profile name from server on update
pullRequest.body:
Closes #8348

## Problem
When a remote profile is refreshed, Config::update_item copies over extra, updated, home, and option, but never touches 
ame. The new name resolved from the server's Content-Disposition header (see PrfItem::from_url) is discarded, so the displayed profile name stays at whatever it was at first import. Users have to delete and re-add the subscription to pick up a renamed airport.

## Change
One line in src-tauri/src/config/profiles.rs: copy item.name onto the existing item during refresh, alongside home/extra/updated.

## Trade-off
Refreshing now adopts the name the server sends. If a user has manually renamed the profile in the UI, the next refresh will overwrite it with the server-provided name. This matches how remote subscriptions behave in similar clients; manual renames are meant to be per-profile overrides that a refresh is allowed to reset.

No local Rust toolchain on this machine; CI will exercise the build.

Assisted by: Claude medium

# Description of Changes

Adds a Troubleshooting entry for losing access to a local database after running `spacetime login`.

Publishing to a local server before logging in (e.g. with `-y`) creates a server-issued identity that owns the database. pullRequest.title: devices: smmuv3: Mirror the RIL and BBML bits
pullRequest.body:
Advertise IDR3 Range-invalidation and Level hint (RIL) and Break-Before-Make behavior Level (BBML) bits based on the host IDR3 value as QEMU advertises the same IDR3 bits: RIL by de206dfd80 ("hw/arm/smmuv3: Advertise SMMUv3.2 range invalidation") and BBML 2 by f8e7163d9e ("hw/arm/smmuv3: Advertise support for SMMUv3.2-BBML2").  This patch doesn't advertise IDR5.VAX as QEMU doesn't.  RIL needs no further support: the emulated SMMUv3 forwards TLBI commands to the host as they are, so the host SMMUv3 executes the guest's range invalidations.

A Linux v6.17+ guest whose CPUs support BBML2 without aborts denies to share its page tables with the SMMU (SVA) unless the SMMU advertises BBML2 (arm_smmu_sva_supported()), and CUDA on a Grace GPU needs that sharing.  This patch makes it work as expected.

pullRequest.title: Bump daemonize to 0.5
pullRequest.body:
0.4.1 pulls in `boxfnonce` which is flagged unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2019-0040). 0.5 dropped that dep.

`exit_action` was removed in 0.5 so the parent-side message handling moves to the `Outcome` returned by `execute()`. Behaviour is the same: the parent waits for the child's "started OK" byte on the unix socket, prints the success/failure line, and exits.

`cargo audit` after the bump still reports daemonize itself as unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2025-0069), but at least the transitive boxfnonce hit is gone.

pullRequest.title: Sync internal, 2026-10-16
stream: preserve unread reset notifications after FIN
pullRequest.body:
RecvBuf::reset() notifies the application of a reset by writing an empty FIN buffer at the final size. When a FIN had already set the final size, write() discarded that buffer, because nothing else needs to be kept from an empty buffer once the final size is known.

A reset that replaced unread data or an unread FIN therefore completed the stream without making it readable. The application never saw the reset, and HTTP/3 kept the request entry until the connection closed.

Insert the empty buffer directly instead, unless the application has already read the FIN or shut down the read side. Since write() no longer checks the final size against the flow control limit, reset() now does so before replacing the receive state.

pullRequest.title: fix(tui): drop the /statusline picker's padding rows when the list doesn't fit
pullRequest.body:
## What and why

The /statusline card keeps a blank padding row above and below its content at every size. When the frame is too short for all eleven items, those two rows go to chrome while items scroll out of view. At 40×12, before:

```
 ┌ Status line ───────────────────────┐
 │                                    │
 │ Choose what the footer shows:      │
 │                                    │
 │  ▸ [✓] Mode  (plan · work ·…)      │
 │    [✓] Model  (the model id…)      │
 │  Space toggle   a all   n none     │
 │  Enter save   Esc cancel           │
 │                                    │
 └────────────────────────────────────┘
```

After:

```
 ┌ Status line ───────────────────────┐
 │ Choose what the footer shows:      │
 │                                    │
 │  ▸ [✓] Mode  (plan · work ·…)      │
 │    [✓] Model  (the model id…)      │
 │    [✓] Context window %  (tokens…) │
 │    [✓] Session cost  (running…)    │
 │  Space toggle   a all   n none     │
 │  Enter save   Esc cancel           │
 └────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The card keeps its vertical padding only when the padded card fits the frame; otherwise it's sized without it. Horizontal padding stays, so the footer still wraps at the width `footer_rows` is computed for. 60×16 goes from six items to eight, and at 80×19, where Git branch used to be cut off, all eleven now show. Row hitboxes are recorded from the content area, so they move with it. Where the list fits, as at 80×24 and 100×32, nothing changes.

## Issue

No-Issue: /statusline spends its padding rows on chrome when items don't fit, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and opened /statusline at 40×12, 60×16, 80×19, 80×20, 80×24 and 100×32, with this change and with a build of d5f6699cc. 80×24 and 100×32 are byte-identical before and after, and 80×20 keeps its padding. At 40×12, End then a click on the Workspace row toggles Workspace.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15349 passed, none failed, including the status picker tests at the blocker sizes and the 40×12 mouse test.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on d5f6699cc; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

pullRequest.title: Add ProgressBar::inc_no_draw()
pullRequest.body:
Adds `ProgressBar::inc_no_draw()`, as suggested by @djc in #706. It only advances the position and skips the `Instant::now()` call and redraw check that `inc()` does on every call, so it is cheaper in hot loops. The new position shows up on the next redraw (`tick()`, `force_draw()`, a steady tick, or a later `inc()`), which the doc comment points out.

I did not add a separate `force_redraw()`, since `ProgressBar::force_draw()` already exists and the doc comment links to it. Happy to rename the method if you prefer something else.

Fixes #706

## Testing

- New `progress_bar_inc_no_draw` test in `tests/render.rs`: the in-memory terminal still shows `0/10` after `inc_no_draw(1)`, and `1/10` after the next `tick()`.
- `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` all pass locally.

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code).

pullRequest.title: channel: Implement Display and Error for TryReadyError and ReadyTimeoutError
pullRequest.body:
`TryReadyError` and `ReadyTimeoutError` are public, re-exported from `crossbeam-channel/src/lib.rs:383`, and are what `Select::try_ready`, `Select::ready_timeout` and `Select::ready_deadline` return. They are the only error types in `crossbeam-channel/src/err.rs` that implement neither `fmt::Display` nor `std::error::Error`, so the select side works and the ready side does not:

```rust
// fine
let _: Box<dyn std::error::Error> = Box::new(crossbeam_channel::SelectTimeoutError);
// error[E0277]: the trait bound `ReadyTimeoutError: std::error::Error` is not satisfied
let _: Box<dyn std::error::Error> = Box::new(crossbeam_channel::ReadyTimeoutError);
```

In practice that means `sel.ready_timeout(d)?` does not compile in a function returning `Box<dyn Error>` or `anyhow::Result`, while `sel.select_timeout(d)?` does, and `println!("{err}")` on either ready error does not compile at all. Today only `Debug` is available, from the `derive` on the two structs.

This adds the two `Display` impls and the two empty `error::Error` impls at the end of `err.rs`, which keeps the impls in the order the types are declared. The messages are the ones already used by the select counterparts at `crossbeam-channel/src/err.rs:340-354`. `TrySelectError` and `TryReadyError` carry the same doc line, "Failed because none of the channel operations were ready.", so both say "all operations in select would block"; `SelectTimeoutError` and `ReadyTimeoutError` carry the same doc line, "Failed because none of the channel operations became ready before the timeout.", so both say "timed out waiting on select".

`error_impls` in `crossbeam-channel/tests/ready.rs` boxes each error as `Box<dyn Error>` and asserts the rendered text. It runs on one thread with no sleeps and no timing assumptions, so it is fine under Miri and on every CI target. `ready_timeout(ms(0))` reaches the deadline branch of `run_ready` deterministically, because `ready_timeout` computes the deadline as `Instant::now()` before the readiness scan and the scan is what advances the clock past it. The sender stays bound as `_s` so the channel is connected and never ready.

Verified on macOS aarch64 with cargo 1.95.0:

- Without the `err.rs` change, `cargo test -p crossbeam-channel --test ready error_impls` fails to build with two `error[E0277]`, one per type.
- With it, `test error_impls ... ok`.
- `cargo test -p crossbeam-channel`: 400 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored across 15 test binaries, plus 74 doctests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p crossbeam-channel --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: clean. `--all-targets` cannot be used on stable here because `benches/crossbeam.rs` opens with `#![feature(test)]`; that fails identically on an unmodified checkout.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

Nothing public is removed or changed, so the addition is backwards compatible.

pullRequest.title: feat(cubestore): Delete orphaned remote files concurrently
pullRequest.body:
**Check List**
- [x] Tests have been run in packages where changes have been made if available
- [x] Linter has been run for changed code
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added if not covered yet
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated if required

## Why

`RemoteFsCleanup` finds `.parquet` files in remote storage that the metastore no longer references and, when `CUBESTORE_ENABLE_REMOVE_ORPHANED_REMOTE_FILES=1`, deletes them. It deletes **one file at a time**, at most `CUBESTORE_REMOTE_FILES_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE` (50k) per pass, one pass an hour.

That is fine for a trickle and useless for a backlog. One Cube Cloud customer has ~19M orphaned files (~65 TB) left by failed pre-aggregation builds; a single pass over their largest bucket already takes ~16 min just to list 8.7M objects. Sequential deletes at that scale take weeks.

## What changes

- `CUBESTORE_REMOTE_FILES_CLEANUP_DELETE_CONCURRENCY` (default **1**, so behaviour is unchanged unless set) runs the deletes of a pass in parallel via `buffer_unordered`.
- The delete phase now stops when the cleanup service is stopped, instead of running a large batch to completion after shutdown.
- New counter `cs.remote_fs.files_removed.count` (tagged like the existing `files_to_remove` gauges) and one info line per pass with how many files were removed, so a drain can be watched.
- First tests for the remote-delete path (`remotefs/cleanup.rs`): with deletion enabled, planted orphans are deleted while referenced files and non-parquet files stay and the table still queries; with it disabled, nothing is deleted.

No change to *what* is considered an orphan: the metastore diff, the `.parquet` filter, the age delay and the re-check against the metastore right before deleting are all as before.

## Context

Cube Cloud turns this on per tenant behind a flag (cubedevinc/cubejs-enterprise PR to follow, pinned to this branch until it merges).

## Verified end to end

On Cube Cloud staging (GCS, 32-way concurrency): 20,050 orphans removed in ~225 s (~89 files/s). 59 live parquet files and 20 orphans younger than the 1 h delay were left untouched, and pre-agg queries kept answering throughout. Details in cubedevinc/cubejs-enterprise#16670.

pullRequest.title: fix(storage): only honor s3 storage class setting for external tables, mark it experimental
pullRequest.body: I hereby agree to the terms of the CLA available at: https://docs.databend.com/dev/policies/cla/ ## Summary The `s3_storage_class` session setting (introduced in #18863) is currently applied to every fuse table, including **internal** tables whose data lives in the bucket configured by the server's `[storage]` section. In a hosted deployment that bucket is owned by the operator, not the end user. A user flipping the setting to `INTELLIGENT_TIERING` would silently add the per-object monitoring fee to storage they neither own nor pay for, with no way for the operator to notice. This PR does two things: 1. **Restrict the user-provided storage class to external tables** (`CREATE TABLE ... 's3://bucket/path' CONNECTION = (...)`), where the bucket is supplied by the user and they can judge from their own access patterns whether intelligent tiering pays off. 2. **Rename the setting to `experimental_s3_storage_class`** to make its status explicit, following the existing `enable_experimental_*` naming convention. The setting has only shipped in nightly builds so far (first in `v1.2.928-nightly`; latest stable is `v1.2.925`), so there is no stable release to stay compatible with. Only the user-facing key and the error message change; the `get_s3_storage_class` getter and internal plumbing keep their names. Behavior after this change: | table kind | `[storage.s3].storage_class` (server config) | `experimental_s3_storage_class` (session setting) | |---|---|---| | internal | honored | **ignored** (was: honored) | | external | n/a (table carries its own params) | honored (unchanged) | | temporary | forced `STANDARD` | forced `STANDARD` (unchanged) | | attached | read-only, never writes new objects | n/a | Implementation: `apply_storage_class` gains an explicit `TableStorageKind` so the policy is decided at the single call site (`create_storage_operator`) that already distinguishes the two cases. The setting description is updated to document the scope. Related: #20689 adds table/database-level `S3_STORAGE_CLASS` options through the same `apply_storage_class` path. After rebasing onto this change those options will also be ignored for internal tables; a follow-up there should reject setting the option on tables without an external location rather than silently ignoring it. ## Tests - [x] Unit Test - [ ] Logic Test - [ ] Benchmark Test - [ ] No Test - _Explain why_ Unit tests in `fuse_table.rs` cover: external table honors specs (upgrade and downgrade), internal table ignores specs in both directions, temp table is always `STANDARD` regardless of kind, non-S3 params are a no-op. No sqllogictest: the storage class does not affect query results and is only observable via S3 `HeadObject`, which the existing MinIO-based logic test environment cannot assert on (MinIO also does not support `INTELLIGENT_TIERING`). No existing test or fixture references the old setting key, so the rename needs no test updates. ## Type of change - [x] Bug Fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New Feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking Change (fix or feature that could cause existing functionality not to work as expected) - [ ] Documentation Update - [ ] Refactoring - [ ] Performance Improvement - [ ] Other (please describe): ## AI assistance - AI usage: A coding agent drafted the change under maintainer direction: locating the single decision point in `create_storage_operator` / `apply_storage_class`, introducing `TableStorageKind`, renaming the setting key, writing the unit tests and doc comments, and running fmt / clippy / unit tests. Scope: `src/query/storages/fuse/src/fuse_table.rs`, `src/query/settings/src/settings_default.rs`, `src/query/settings/src/settings_getter_setter.rs`. - Responsible human: @dantengsky - [x] The responsible human has read every line of this diff and can explain each change - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/databendlabs/databend/20721)

pullRequest.title: Add `PgConnection::version`
pullRequest.body:
Third of the stacked series started in https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/pull/5295, based on https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/pull/5296.

`PgConnection::version` reads `PQserverVersion`, which libpq caches at connection startup, so it needs no query. It decodes both numbering schemes, three-part releases before PostgreSQL 10 and `major.minor` since, which it reports with a patch of zero. A broken connection makes `PQserverVersion` return zero, which surfaces as `DatabaseErrorKind::ClosedConnection`.

pullRequest.title: add exceptional shift
pullRequest.body:
### Summary of Changes
This PR fixes some cases where the search for eigenvalue could hang. This was solved by using the "Exceptional Shift" method in Wilkinson, J. H., & Reinsch, C. (1971). 
Handbook for automatic computation (Vol. 2: Linear algebra). 

### Details
I first checked why the Lapack algorithm would converge and not hang. I looked at dlahqr procedure (https://netlib.org/lapack/explore-html/d8/df4/group__lahqr_ga100049ab080cef756846702a33e8e28f.html) saw the mention of the exceptional shift and the Ahues & Tisseur stopping criterion.

The last one was a red herring, I implemented it but the test matrix from #611 would still hang. I then implemented the exceptional shift and it worked. I tried tracing back the magical value (0.75 & -0.4375), and discovered https://www.netlib.org/eispack/hqr.f that led me to the original source:

Wilkinson, J. H., & Reinsch, C. (1971). 
Handbook for automatic computation (Vol. 2: Linear algebra).

You can view the orignal magical number and algorithm implementation here : https://www.scribd.com/document/568239788/Wilkinson-Reinsch1971-Book-HandbookForAutomaticComputatio#page=373
 
AI was used to find the original paper

### Testing
I implemented a test with the matrix from #611 that now pass successfully

Fixes #611

When `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set to a relative path, `find_target_dir` gave up and returned `Unknown`, so the shared `cxxbridge` directory went to the scratch location instead of the target dir. pullRequest.title: Release 0.37.0 - Color emojis
Fix lost condvar wakeup on mt worker shutdown
pullRequest.body:
Fixes the worker hanging on shutdown in the `mt` arm of `src/serve.rs`.

The shutdown thread waited on the condvar without checking the flag. The runtime task sets the flag and calls `notify_one()`. If it gets there first, the notification is lost, because `std::sync::Condvar` does not store one. The thread then sleeps forever, `release()` is never called, the Python loop never returns, and granian SIGKILLs the worker on `workers-kill-timeout`.

It now waits in a loop over the flag. `wait_while` would do the same in one line if you prefer that.

Without the fix the reproduction from #875 hung in every run, first hang between 105s and 795s. With it, nothing in 384 restarts over eight runs of 15 minutes.

I also built the branch with a three second sleep in that window to widen it. Without the fix the first restart hung, with the fix none of 40 did.

Fixes #900, the full write-up is there.

pullRequest.title: fix(render): coerce numeric and boolean echo params
pullRequest.body:
Fixes #2722.

## The problem

A numeric `global_vars` entry fails to render, with an error that says the parameter is missing when it is right there:

```yaml
global_vars:
  - name: myvar
    type: echo
    params:
      echo: 12345
```

The YAML loader is doing the right thing: an unquoted `12345` is a YAML integer, so `convert_value` produces `Value::Number(Number::Integer(12345))` (`espanso-config/src/matches/group/loader/yaml/util.rs:44`). But the echo extension only ever matched `Value::String`:

```rust
if let Some(Value::String(echo)) = params.get("echo") {
```

so anything else fell to the `else` and reported `missing 'echo' parameter`. The user has to know to quote the value, and the error points them nowhere near that.

I confirmed the three cases before touching anything:

```
number   => Error(missing 'echo' parameter)
bool     => Error(missing 'echo' parameter)
string   => Success(Single("12345"))
```

@smeech noted in the thread that this is intentional YAML behaviour and that coercion is what's actually wanted here, the way `replace:` values already get coerced. This PR does exactly that, for `echo` only — `date`'s `offset:` still needs a real number, so I left it alone.

## The fix

Match numbers and booleans too, formatting each explicitly:

- `Number::Integer` / `Number::Float` via `to_string()` — shortest round-trip, so `0.1` stays `0.1` and `1e20` expands in full with no precision loss
- `Bool` as `true` / `false`

`Null`, `Array` and `Object` still error. `Null` is what a bare `echo:` produces, and rendering it as `null` would be worse than failing; arrays and objects have no sensible single-string form, and formatting them via `Debug` would leak Rust syntax into the user's text.

`schemas/match.schema.json` is widened to `["string", "number", "boolean"]` in the same commit, otherwise the editor extensions would keep red-underlining exactly the config this makes valid.

One thing worth knowing: `Number::Float(1.0)` renders as `1`, not `1.0`. That's Rust's float formatting and it's pinned in the tests so it isn't a surprise later.

## Tests

Two new tests alongside the existing ones: `echo_coerces_scalars` covers integers (including negative), floats (`1.0` and `1.5`), and both booleans; `echo_rejects_non_scalars` pins that `Null`/`Array`/`Object` keep erroring.

pullRequest.title: Upgrade wasmtime to v49
pullRequest.body:
## Summary

Upgrades `wasmtime` and `wasmtime-wasi` from 48 to 49 (resolves to 49.0.1).

- `runtime/Cargo.toml`: `wasmtime` and `wasmtime-wasi` `48` → `49`. No source changes are needed. Every wasmtime feature the runtime enables (`anyhow`, `cache`, `gc`, `gc-drc`, `cranelift`, `coredump`, `wat`, `parallel-compilation`, `pooling-allocator`, `demangle`) still exists in 49.
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: `1.95.0` → `1.96.0`. Wasmtime 49 (and `wasmtime-wasi` 49) declare `rust-version = 1.96.0`.

## Validation

Ran the same checks CI runs, locally on macOS (aarch64):

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --all --release --all-features --no-deps -- -D "clippy::all"`: clean
- `cargo test --release` / `--all-features` / `--no-default-features`: all pass, except for one flaky timing test (below)
- `cargo check -p extism --no-default-features`: builds

## Reviewer notes

**`test_disable_cache` is flaky on 48 too.** This test checks that loading a tiny module from the compilation cache is faster than compiling it with the cache turned off. When the whole suite runs in parallel, CPU contention can flip that comparison. I timed it on both versions:

| | Isolated: cached / uncached | Full suite under load |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wasmtime 48 | ~6.5ms / ~13ms | one run had cached 34.2ms vs uncached 25.0ms (assertion fails) |
| Wasmtime 49 | ~6–8ms / ~13–23ms | occasionally fails the same way |

The cache still gives about a 2× speedup on 49, so this isn't a regression. The test isn't changed here; making it robust is separate work.

**LTS consideration.** extism/extism#912 moved to Wasmtime 48 specifically because it is an LTS release that gets security backports. 49 isn't LTS, so this moves Extism off the LTS line until the next LTS release. Worth deciding whether that trade-off is acceptable before merging.

pullRequest.body:
## What

The start menu always opens on the favorites view: `onTriggered` resets `globalState.view` to `StartView.Favorites` every time it is shown. People who prefer the full app list have to click "All apps" on every open.

This adds a widget setting to choose the view shown when the menu opens:

- **Favorites** (default, current behavior)
- **All apps**

## How

- `src/static/widgets/apps-menu/metadata.yml`: new `select` setting `defaultView` (`favorites` | `all`), `defaultValue: favorites`, same pattern as the settings of `@seelen/flyouts` and `@seelen/task-switcher`.
- `state/mod.svelte.ts`: `globalState.defaultView` reads it with `settings.value.getCurrentWidgetConfig()`. Any value other than `all` falls back to favorites.
- `state/positioning.svelte.ts`: `onTriggered` sets `globalState.view = globalState.defaultView` instead of the hardcoded favorites. The "All apps" / "Back" button and the search (which still jumps to all apps) work as before.
- Labels in `i18n/settings/default-view*.yml`, translated with the repo's `GoogleTranslator`.

## Tested

Local debug build on Windows 11:

- `byWidget["@seelen/apps-menu"].defaultView = "all"`: the menu opens directly on the full app list, with the "Back" button.
- Without the setting: the menu opens on favorites, as before.

Not tested: changing the option from the Settings UI (only by editing `settings.json`).

`deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `svelte-check` and `cargo test` pass, and the CI passed on my fork.

pullRequest.title: fix(msl): set the metal shader language version when in passthrough mode
pullRequest.body:
## Connections
I encountered this problem when working with CubeCL's metal backend. However, I was not able to identify an existing issue for it.

## Description
Currently the appropriate metal shader language is detected, but only specified to the underlying MSL compiler when translating WGSL to MSL. This means that passthrough mode gets an unspecified version. In my case that resulted in failed compilations, because the default version on macOS 26.6 ended up being lower than 3.2, while the WGSL path would have chosen MSL 4.

Solved in 1-line by setting the already detected MSL compiler version on the Metal passthrough path as well:
```rust
  let options = MTLCompileOptions::new();
+ options.setLanguageVersion(self.shared.private_caps.msl_version);
```

## Testing

I've run `WGPU_BACKEND=metal cargo xtask test -E 'binary(wgpu-gpu) & test(metal_passthrough_shader)'`

However, this change is so small it should be easy to tell if there are any other possible ramifications.

## LLM Use?
An LLM identified the bug and found the fix. However, all writing is my own.

pullRequest.title: Point Dialog::important_area at the focused button
pullRequest.body:
Fixes #813.

`Dialog::important_area()` always returned the content's area, even when a button
had focus - there was a `// TODO: if a button is focused, return the button
position instead.` sitting on that line. So a `ScrollView` wrapping a tall
`Dialog` scrolled to the content and stopped, and the buttons below stayed
unreachable once focus moved to them.

Now it matches on `self.focus`: content focus keeps the existing calculation,
button focus asks the focused button for its important area and translates it by
the offset the button already records. That is the same shape `FixedLayout`,
`LinearLayout` and `ListView` use for their focused child.

The test lays out and draws a 20x5 dialog with two buttons and asserts the
important area for all three focus states. Coordinates are hardcoded rather than
derived from `offset`/`size`, so it cannot just restate the implementation - I
checked it fails on master and on the plausible wrong versions (hardcoded button
index; adding `borders + padding` to the button arm by symmetry with the content
arm).

Two things worth flagging:

- Button offsets are written in `draw_buttons()`, not in `layout()`, so before
  the first draw they are still zero. In practice focus only reaches a button
  after an event, and `run()` refreshes before the first `step()`, so the offsets
  are current by then; the degenerate case is a scroll to the top for one frame,
  not a panic. It is the same contract `check_focus_grab()` already relies on for
  mouse hit-testing. Moving the button positioning into `layout()` would remove
  the hazard, but it duplicates the alignment math and felt like more than this
  fix needed - say the word if you would prefer it.
- This only covers the buttons half of your comment on #813. The border is still
  excluded from the important area, which is consistent with the content arm but
  means the bottom border row can stay clipped. Happy to include it if that is
  what you want.

`cargo fmt`, `clippy` and the full test suite are clean. Two files, `theme.rs`
and `backends/curses/n.rs`, are already rustfmt-dirty on master; I left those
alone.

Written with AI assistance; I reproduced the bug, verified the fix and ran the
tests myself.

pullRequest.title: Navigate to fragments in the same document
pullRequest.body:
## What changed

Fixes #1286.

Fragment navigation now follows the HTML spec in `bootstrap.js`:

- `Location` gets setters for `hash`, `search`, `pathname`, `host`, `hostname` and `port`. Each changes one part of a copy of the current URL and navigates to it. Before, only getters existed, so `location.hash = 'x'` was silently dropped (or threw `TypeError` in strict code).
- `location.href`, `assign`, `replace`, `window.location = …` and `document.location = …` go through one helper. A target that has a fragment and otherwise equals the current URL becomes a same-document navigation: no document load, a new history entry (`replace` replaces the current one), and a queued `hashchange` with `oldURL`/`newURL` when the fragment changed. Any other target loads as before.
- Script `.click()` on `<a href="#x">` now activates the link instead of being skipped.

The history entry is added inside the existing History IIFE (through `__obscuraNavigateToFragment`), so `history.length`, `history.back()` and the `__virtualUrl` that backs `page.url()` stay consistent with `pushState`.

Out of scope: `location.protocol` stays read-only. `pushState` still fires `hashchange` when only the fragment differs (existing behavior; Chrome doesn't).

## Validation

New tests in `crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs`:

- `location_hash_navigates_to_a_fragment_in_the_same_document`: `location.hash`, `location.href = '#…'` and `<a>.click()` keep the document (no pending navigation, page globals survive), add history entries, fire `hashchange` in order, and `history.back()` returns to the previous fragment. Setting the same fragment again is a no-op.
- `location_replace_with_a_fragment_replaces_the_history_entry`
- `location_component_setters_load_the_new_url`: `search` and `pathname` setters queue a normal navigation.

`obscura-js` lib tests, each in its own process (nextest isn't installed here, so I ran every test binary entry separately with `--exact`):

pullRequest.title: Tile lhs rows in the generic CPU quantized matmul for prefill
pullRequest.body:
k_quants::matmul, the CPU quantized matmul used whenever no repacked kernel applies, looped over the input rows and dispatched the weight column quads to the thread pool once per row. With m prefill rows every weight block was re-read m times and the pool dispatched m times, so rows/s at m = 128 was the same as at m = 1 (581 vs 587 rows/s for a 38 MB Q4K 8184x8192 weight on a 4-core Xeon).

Keep the m == 1 decode path as is and, for m > 1, run a single chunked dispatch over (row tile, column quad) work items, row-tile major, with tiles of 16 rows (ggml's src1 row block). A worker walking its range keeps the quantized lhs tile in cache and streams each weight quad once per tile instead of once per row. Every output element is still produced by the same vec_dot call on the same inputs, only the loop order changes, so results are bit-identical to the previous code.

For weights larger than the LLC this gives ~1.45x rows/s at m >= 32 on the generic path (Q4K 38 MB: 587 -> 833 rows/s, Q8_0 71 MB: 273 -> 396); for LLC-resident weights the path is bound by the per-element vec_dot kernel and the gain is 0-25%. The repacked paths are untouched.

Add a test that checks, for every GGML type and several m, that the batched output equals the single-row output exactly, and an ignored timing harness for the prefill shapes.

pullRequest.title: feat(pricing): scope custom rates by billing provider
pullRequest.body:
Add pricing rules scoped to the billing provider recorded in logs, while preserving the existing global `models` configuration in `custom-pricing.json`. Raw model identity, billing identity, cache migration, and local pricing explanations use the same selection logic.

## Why

Existing global rules can apply one gateway's rates to the same model on other channels. The attribution provider alone cannot distinguish the actual billing channel, so matching uses an explicitly recorded billing identity and remains Unknown when evidence is missing.

## Changes

- Add a `provider_overrides` array with precedence scoped raw → global raw → scoped synthetic-normalized → global synthetic-normalized. Billing provider matching only trims surrounding whitespace and normalizes ASCII case; it does not guess aliases or infer a channel from the model vendor.
- Use one selected pricing row for cost, coverage, source, and multipliers, without filling missing rates from other rows. Explicit zero rates remain distinct from no match, and provider-reported amounts, including zero, take precedence.
- Migrate legacy caches while preserving historical tokens, authoritative amounts, and MiCode provenance. Backfill identity from existing source files, retain original records when backfill fails, and never overwrite a damaged shard with empty contents. Recalculate previous estimates using the current configuration.
- Add CLI `--billing-provider`, `--source`, strict override-configuration validation, and local `pricing explain`. Private channel labels and explanation fields do not enter public submission payloads.
- Include a schema, examples, maintained README translations, and synthetic compatibility fixtures.

## Implementation

Billing identity is stored separately from the attribution provider used for grouping and upstream lookups; raw and display models are also kept separate. Unknown identities can still use global rules and existing upstream resolution. The compatibility fallback for legacy global parser aliases does not broaden scoped matching. Existing complete-free pricing policy and Zed/OpenAI multiplier behavior are preserved.

## Verification

- Cloud Linux validation on the final tree `f3968920d5ef5540c3f4538f0285607a3588cbc5` (Rust 1.98.0): `cargo test --locked --offline --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast` passed 4586 tests, with 0 failures and 5 ignored tests. One nested subprocess test is not counted twice.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --offline --no-deps --workspace` each completed with exit code 0 on that final source.
- Regression tests cover advisor billing after duplicate, retained-history, warm-cache and cross-file parent changes; Jcode snapshot/journal route boundaries and corrections; FX raw model keys; ordinary deleted Claude sessions; and opaque CLI billing labels that must not affect upstream catalog selection. Legacy cache fixtures, authoritative zero amounts, partial custom coverage, schema/runtime parity and hosted multipliers remain covered.
- Frozen cache source files retain LF bytes on Windows. Fixture comparisons use explicit UTC without regenerating historical payloads or changing process-global TZ. Independent runs of the final binary passed four cache-fixture tests, one provenance test and three advisor lifecycle tests in seven timezones, including UTC+14, UTC−12 and Kathmandu (56 test executions). Restoring the source patch onto its recorded base reproduced the final tree exactly.
- GitHub Actions for [`2d03d774`](https://github.com/huyanxius/tokscale/commit/2d03d774c62b59f49da1008daedefc64d44102cf) passed [Windows and Ubuntu tests, strict lint, and Rustdoc](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/actions/runs/38949605393), [all nine native build targets](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/actions/runs/38949605298), [Launcher Validation](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/actions/runs/38949605084), [TUI Container CI](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/actions/runs/38949605462), and [Release Validation](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/actions/runs/38949604995). The separate coverage-report job was skipped.

## Risks

The implementation includes upstream through `ba1d32801e385f8e19830cc430e9c6d84344a3e2`, including #1431's cache/context changes and #1422's cost provenance. Legacy Codex state is decoded using its frozen historical layout. Cost, coverage and provenance use the same selected pricing row; an unsupported zero estimate remains Unknown. Claude retention generations preserve older provenance while rebuilding live billing metadata, and advisors follow the final parent identity after aggregation without replacing authoritative amounts.

Older binaries ignore `provider_overrides`, so downgrading can change estimates. Copilot cache envelopes are versioned to prevent the new message layout from being decoded as the old positional format. A channel label in a log does not verify the actual merchant, account or endpoint; different endpoints recorded under the same label cannot be distinguished. Jcode's mutable snapshot-wide route cannot establish historical billing identity; only a journal batch's own metadata establishes scope for newly observed message IDs, and later corrections preserve their first-observed identity.

## Scope

This PR implements provider-scoped pricing for #902. Within the current roots, missing-source Claude entries survive only when they hold retained compacted history or pre-provenance legacy history whose retained subset cannot be identified. Ordinary deleted, uncompacted Claude sessions and missing sources for other clients are pruned. Failed identity backfills preserve the original records, and damaged shards are not overwritten with empty contents. Subscription bills, taxes, discounts and historical effective dates are outside this scope.

## Related Issues

Closes #902

pullRequest.title: fix(python): reject blob ranges unsupported by storage schemas
pullRequest.body:
Python row conversion builds blob arrays with the table's storage schema. Columns upgraded from legacy blob fields can contain only `data` and `uri`, so PyArrow silently discarded requested `position` and `size` values and stored whole-file references.

Reject non-null range fields that the storage schema cannot represent before constructing the Arrow array. The error identifies the column and explains how to create a range-capable schema with `lancedb.blob()`. Whole-file references, inline bytes, and null values remain supported on minimal schemas; full blob schemas continue to preserve ranges.

Regression coverage exercises dictionaries and `Blob.from_uri()` in Python lists and pandas DataFrames, offsets of zero and four, atomic rejection on minimal schemas, and byte-accurate reads on full schemas.

Validation:
- Confirmed the regression fails on the original code because the write does not raise an error.
- `cd python && uv run --extra tests pytest python/tests/test_blob.py -q`: 171 passed, 1 skipped.
- Python Ruff lint and formatting pass. Repository-wide Ruff reports existing failures in unchanged CI and documentation files; unrelated formatter changes were excluded.

Fixes #4563

pullRequest.title: vello_cpu: Fix `Color` and `Luminosity` blends turning some grays black
pullRequest.body: Fixes #1999. `clip_color` divides by `l - n` when `n < 0` and by `x - l` when `x > 1`, without checking the denominator. After `set_lum`, a gray has three equal components, so `l == n == x`. When rounding leaves them just below 0 (or just above 1), the division is 0/0. The NaN survives `apply_alpha`, even over a transparent backdrop, and packs to black. With `Mix::Color` and `Mix::Luminosity`, some gray levels come out black in both pipelines. This PR clips only where the denominator is positive: `n < 0 && l - n > 0` and `x > 1 && x - l > 0`. For a neutral color, the clipped value's limit is the color itself, so skipping the clip loses nothing. Skia (`l != mn`, `l != mx`) and pixman (`FLOAT_IS_ZERO(l - n)`) guard the same case. `vello_gpu_shaders/shaders/helpers/blend.wesl` and `research/vello_shaders/shader/shared/blend.wgsl` have the same unguarded `clip_color` and get the same guard. I couldn't make the GPU path produce black pixels on Metal, but WGSL gives an indeterminate value for a division without a finite result, so the guard still helps there. ## Testing - New snapshot tests `mix_luminosity_gray_ramp` (black at 50% over every opaque gray) and `mix_color_gray_ramp` (every gray at 50% alpha over a transparent target). Without the guard, the first renders 9 cells black in the f32 pipeline, and the second 2 cells in the u8 pipeline and 9 in the f32 pipeline. Both pass with the guard. - `cargo test -p vello_cpu` passes. - `cargo test -p vello_tests --release` passes on CPU and on GPU (Metal, Apple M3 Max), with no changes to existing snapshots. - `cargo test -p vello_gpu_shaders --all-features` passes. `vello_gpu_shaders` and `vello_shaders` build, and their build scripts validate the WGSL with naga. - The reproducer from the issue now reports 0 black pixels for every mode in both render modes. - `cargo fmt --check`, `typos`, the CI clippy commands for `vello_cpu` and `vello_tests` (including `no_std` and wasm32), and the 1.89 MSRV check are clean. ### Before and after Renders of the two new snapshot tests from vello_cpu, scaled 4x. Each 6x6 cell is one gray level, 0 to 255, 16 to a row. The two `Color` images have a checkerboard behind them, so a cell that should be a light translucent gray but came out translucent black is easy to spot. `mix_luminosity_gray_ramp`, f32 pipeline: black at 50% over every opaque gray. Before the fix, levels 45, 77, 90, 127, 154, 180, 193, 245 and 254 render black. `mix_color_gray_ramp`, f32 pipeline: every gray at 50% alpha over a transparent target. The same nine levels render as translucent black. `mix_color_gray_ramp`, u8 pipeline: levels 233 and 234 render as translucent black.

pullRequest.title: editor: Tell a custom context menu whether it was opened on the gutter
pullRequest.body: ## Description A right-click on a line number opens the text's menu today — Cut, Copy, Paste — and moves the caret there. An editor that wants a menu about the line clicked — bookmark it, toggle a breakpoint, accept a change in a diff — has no way to tell that the click was on the gutter, nor which row. This tells the menu, and keeps every existing builder working as it does. `examples/editor_gutter_menu` shows it: a line number's menu bookmarks (a `GutterMarker::Bookmark` through a line decoration provider), selects or copies the line, and the text keeps the usual menu. The input page and the editor page describe it, in English and Chinese. Stacked on #3520 (`hit_test`), whose two commits the diff here still shows; the diff to review is the last three commits. Once #3520 lands it will be rebased onto `next`. ## Screenshot | a line number's menu, the selection kept | after Bookmark Line 6 | the text's menu | |---|---|---| | | | | Drawn headless on Linux, where the native menu falls back to the drawn popup. ## Public API ### gpui-component (`gpui_kit::component::input`) - `Input::context_menu_with(self, f: impl Fn(NativeMenu, InputContextMenuCapabilities, Option, &mut Window, &mut App) -> NativeMenu + 'static) -> Self` and `Editor::context_menu_with`, the same — a builder that receives the capabilities and what the right-click was over, from `hit_test` (#3520): the text at an offset, or a row of the gutter in a column. `context_menu` keeps its signature and is now the builder that ignores them. - `default_context_menu(menu: NativeMenu, capabilities: InputContextMenuCapabilities) -> NativeMenu` — the built-in items, public, for the clicks a custom builder leaves alone. - `InputContextMenuCapabilities` — re-exported from `gpui-base`, for the two signatures above. ### gpui-base (`gpui_kit::base::input`, re-exported by `gpui_kit::component::input`) - `InputBaseState::gutter_context_menu_moves_cursor(self, moves: bool) -> Self` / `InputBaseState::set_gutter_context_menu_moves_cursor(&mut self, moves: bool)` — `true` by default, as now; `false` keeps the selection while the gutter's menu is open (and skips the hover-definition lookup for it). - `#[doc(hidden)] InputBaseState::on_context_menu_with_hit(&mut self, handler: Rc, Point, &mut Window, &mut App)>)` — how `Input` hands the hit to its builder, as `set_editor_paddings` hands over the paddings; `on_context_menu` keeps its signature. ## How to Test - `a_right_click_on_the_gutter_tells_the_menu_its_row` (base) — the gutter's row and column reach the menu; by default the caret moves to the row, with the flag off the selection stays, and the text moves the caret either way. - `a_menu_built_with_its_target_knows_the_row_of_the_gutter` (component) — through `Editor::context_menu_with` the builder sees the gutter's row and the text's, and `context_menu` still opens. Each goes red with its protection removed: the hit left out of the menu's handler, the flag ignored, the hit dropped between `Input` and the builder. - `cargo test -p gpui-base --lib -- input::` (362 passed), `cargo test -p gpui-component --lib -- input::` (45 passed) - `cargo run -p example-editor-gutter-menu` — drawn headless, screenshots above ## Checklist - [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md) document and followed the guidelines. - [x] Reviewed the changes in this PR and confirmed AI generated code (If any) is accurate. - [ ] Passed `cargo run` for story tests related to the changes. - [x] Tested macOS, Windows and Linux platforms performance (if the change is platform-specific)

python.lsh: Avoid capturing underscores as numeric literals
pullRequest.body:
The definition of numeric literals in `python.lsh` currently captures underscores, so identifiers like `__init__` and `._foo` are considered to be numeric literals immediately followed by identifiers and are discarded as invalid.

I've changed the regex for numeric literals by replacing `[\d_]+` with `\d[\d_]*`.

pullRequest.title: Send keepalive pings on user websockets to survive idle proxy timeouts
pullRequest.body:
Cloudflare closes TCP sockets that go quiet, and our two user-facing sockets `/ws/update` and `/ws/terminal`, send nothing while idle. The socket sits there until the proxy reaps it and the UI falls back to its reconnect loop. 

This PR makes the server send a WebSocket Ping every 30s on both endpoints. 

(Core<->Periphery connections already ping every 5s. This only touches the two browser-facing endpoints.)

## Files
  - `bin/core/src/api/ws/mod.rs` - shared `WS_KEEP_ALIVE_INTERVAL` (30s)
  - `bin/core/src/api/ws/update.rs` - ping in the update send loop
  - `bin/core/src/api/ws/terminal.rs` - ping in the terminal forward loop

pullRequest.title: Fixing formatting issues
Entity-level code map via sem-core (#315)
pullRequest.body:
Implements the entity-level code map from #315. Thanks for the enthusiastic green light @ODAncona, excited to land this.

## What it does

With `--entity-map`, code2prompt extracts each file's structural entities (functions, classes, methods) with line ranges and signatures via [sem-core](https://crates.io/crates/sem-core), and renders a compact outline before the file contents. So a prompt can lead with the shape of the codebase instead of making the model infer it from full files.

Example output:

```
Code Map:

`math.py`:
  - class Calculator `class Calculator:` (lines 1-7)
  - function add `def add(self, a, b):` (lines 3-4)
  - function main `def main():` (lines 9-11)
```

## Design decisions (the ones flagged in the issue)

- **Placement:** both. Per-file via `FileEntry.entities`, plus a top-level `code_map` aggregate, since the data is useful both ways and costs nothing to expose twice.
- **Format:** structured data is the source of truth (name, kind, line range, signature, parent); a default Handlebars partial renders the indented tree, so templates that want a signature-only or custom view can build it.
- **Default + flag:** off by default, opt in with `--entity-map` / `Code2PromptConfig.entity_map`.
- **Build cost:** sem-core carries tree-sitter grammars for ~28 languages, so it is an **optional dependency behind the `entity-map` Cargo feature**. Standard builds are unaffected.
- **Privacy:** sem-core is the offline library and emits no telemetry (that lives only in the sem CLI binary, not the crate), so code2prompt stays fully air-gapped. Quick proof: `grep -r reqwest` in sem-core returns nothing.

## Try it

```
cargo run -p code2prompt --features entity-map -- /path/to/repo --entity-map
```

## Tests

Unit tests for Rust and Python extraction (feature-gated); full suite passes with and without the feature; verified end to end on a mixed sample.

## Scope

This is the code map. The natural follow-up is function-level context forging (pull a function plus its real callers/callees across files, token-budgeted, via sem's dependency graph), which is the bigger token-savings win. Happy to do that as a second PR once this lands.

pullRequest.title: fix(iroh): update local addresses on network change
pullRequest.body:
## Description

Fixes #4588

The idea is to directly update addresses (`update_direct_addresses`) in `re_stun` when we get network changes and have no relays to probe. Since this can only happen in non-WASM environments, the code block is gated.

To confirm this works, I used the branch https://github.com/ok300/iroh/tree/ok300-fix-stale-direct-addrs-repro , which contains:
- c1bdad044b1282fd27a553ef6dcbf83ce3f607f3 = this PR's change
- 21bc62bfbae3c3c917fd17709663f73d6a6aecd9 = the repro test proposed by @guillemcordoba in the original issue's description

```
$ cargo run --example stale-direct-addrs

  0.0 s  advertised [192.168.64.5]
  2.4 s  advertised [127.0.0.1, ::1]   // Printed as soon as I turned WiFi off
  3.6 s  advertised [192.168.64.5]     // Printed as soon as I turned WiFi on
```

## API Changes

n/a

## Notes & open questions

I tried to avoid the `#[cfg(not(wasm_browser))]` gating, but couldn't get around it because `update_direct_addresses` itself needs it.

I'm aware there are more broader, more comprehensive solutions discussed at https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh/issues/4588#issuecomment-6038427842 . However I tried to keep the fix minimal and non-invasive.

I also explored calling `update_direct_addresses` from `handle_network_change`, as an idea proposed in the comment linked above. However an AI advised against it, see details below:

<details>

The alternative (`handle_network_change`) has incomplete coverage.

`re_stun` is called from 5 different locations:
- Line 1535: Periodic timer tick → `re_stun(Periodic)`
- Line 1592: Portmap external address changed → `re_stun(PortmapUpdated)`
- Line 1668: Major link change → `re_stun(LinkChangeMajor)`
- Line 1670: Minor link change → `re_stun(LinkChangeMinor)`
- Line 1760: Relay map changed → `re_stun(RelayMapChange)`

The alternative in `handle_network_change` only covers cases 3 & 4 (link changes from netmon). It would miss:
- Periodic updates: Even without relays, we want periodic refresh of local addresses (interfaces can change without netmon events)
- Portmap updates: Portmapper can discover new external addresses independently
- Relay map transitions: When `relay_map` changes from empty→non-empty or vice versa
</details>

## Change checklist

- [x] Documentation updates following the [style guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/1574-more-api-documentation-conventions.html#appendix-a-full-conventions-text), if relevant.
- [x] Tests if relevant.
- [x] All API changes documented.

pullRequest.title: chore(deps): Update Rust crate gix to 0.89.0
pullRequest.body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [gix](https://redirect.github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide) | dependencies | minor | `0.88.0` → `0.89.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>GitoxideLabs/gitoxide (gix)</summary>

### [`v0.89.0`](https://redirect.github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/releases/tag/gix-v0.89.0): gix v0.89.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/compare/gix-v0.88.0...gix-v0.89.0)

##### Reverted (BREAKING)

- replace `fs` with `gix-fs`

  <!-- agent -->

  `gix-fs` already provides the filesystem helpers and recursive walkers.
  Keeping their duplicate implementation in `gix-features` adds unnecessary
  filesystem dependencies to the foundational feature crate.

  Remove the `fs` module and the `walkdir` and `fs-read-dir` features. Migrate
  workspace callers to `gix_fs`, move traversal requests to `gix-fs/walkdir`,
  and update the manifests, lockfile, traversal documentation, and feature
  check script together.

##### Changed (BREAKING)

- use `gix::Result` throughout the public API

  <!-- agent -->

  The error migration left public `gix` methods, iterators, callbacks, and
  configuration validators returning a mixture of exceptions, I/O errors,
  custom error enums, and even the rejected input itself. Callers still had
  to adapt these separately despite the common `gix::Error` boundary.

  Use the crate-level `Result` throughout APIs defined by `gix`, including
  fallible configuration inputs and owned `TryFrom` implementations. Keep
  underlying causes, classifications, and diagnostic metadata available
  through `gix::Error`. Configuration adapters accept arbitrary caller errors
  without panicking or losing their causes. Object kind conversions report
  validation errors. Re-exported plumbing APIs and error types required by
  external traits retain their existing contracts.

  Adapt `gitoxide-core` and `gix-tix` callers in the same breaking change,
  removing explicit conversions that became identities.

##### New Features

- remove linked worktrees safely

  <!-- agent -->

  Expose safe linked-worktree removal through `gix`, using the `gix-worktree`
  removal plumbing. Validate the selected worktree, inspect dirty and locked
  states, and preserve the checkout unless the requested removal policy permits
  deleting it.

  Enable removal through `worktree-mutation` and report progress and cleanup
  outcomes to callers. Keep branch deletion explicit, adding compare-and-swap
  branch removal for callers that have already inspected a target so concurrent
  branch changes are not lost. Cover porcelain removal behavior and conditional
  branch deletion in disposable repositories.
- add and check out linked worktrees

  <!-- agent -->

  Expose `Repository::add_worktree()` for existing local branches and detached
  commits. Prepare the links, initialize `HEAD` and its reflog, check out
  the commit, and write the index, rolling back created files on failure or
  interruption.

  Inherit worktree configuration and common attributes before checkout. Enumerate
  the main and linked repositories consistently so additions and branch deletion
  protect branches checked out or reserved by bisect and rebase, while matching
  Git's default namespace behavior.

  Support `worktree.useRelativePaths` with its repository-format upgrade and
  `extensions.relativeWorktrees` validation. Compare behavior with Git for
  bare parents, separate Git directories, moved relative links, configuration
  inheritance, invalid destinations, and rollback.

  Format already-registered worktree destinations with `Path::display()`.

##### Bug Fixes

- honor section trust when merging submodule overrides

  <!-- agent -->

  A report describes reduced-trust repository configuration overriding
  submodule settings, including command-valued updates. Apply the repository's
  existing configurable section filter for worktree, index, and HEAD module
  sources, and retain each copied section's origin metadata.

  Keep trusted API overrides usable and restrict module enumeration to the
  original module definitions. The regressions first reproduced both the trust
  bypass and lost provenance, then covered custom filters and every source.

  Git reference: `setup.c::ensure_valid_ownership`, `submodule-config.c`, and
  `builtin/submodule--helper.c` at `d38352cd43ab9745686d697872408bc3249a153f`
  distinguish shared module definitions from trusted local overrides.
- read the target reflog when a symbolic ref has no log

  <!-- agent -->

  Reflog specifications such as `refs/symref@{0}` failed when the symbolic
  reference had no log of its own, even though its final target had one.

  Follow symbolic references only when their own reflog is absent, retaining
  precedence of an existing log. Reuse the reference-following helper for
  chained references, cycle detection, and missing-ref errors.
  The regression compares indexed and dated queries, chained references,
  and existing-log precedence against isolated Git invocations in a
  disposable repository.

  Git reference: `/Users/byron/dev/github.com/git/git`,
  `refs.c::repo_dwim_log()` prefers a reference's own log, then its resolved
  target's log. Runtime comparisons used Git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157).
- resolve `HEAD` tracking branches through the current branch

  <!-- agent -->

  `Repository::rev_parse_single()` rejected `HEAD@{upstream}`, `HEAD@{u}`,
  and `HEAD@{push}` because it looked for tracking configuration on `HEAD`
  instead of the currently checked out branch.

  Follow `HEAD` before looking up tracking configuration, reusing the existing
  symbolic-reference resolution helper and retaining missing-ref errors.
  The regression compares all three tracking aliases with their implicit
  forms and isolated Git invocations in a disposable repository.

  Git reference: `/Users/byron/dev/github.com/git/git`,
  `remote.c::repo_branch_get()` treats `HEAD` as the current branch.
  Runtime comparisons used Git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157).
- match equivalent Windows paths when removing worktrees
  The Windows fast-test job failed in Tix associated-branch cleanup:
  `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...\topic` was reported as not registered even
  though Git had created the worktree. Git can record the long-name path,
  while callers retain a short-name or verbatim path for the same directory.
  The shared-base removal resolver only compared path components after
  symlink resolution, which does not expand Windows short names.

  After the existing component comparison fails on Windows, compare
  canonical paths when both exist. Apply this at the shared equality helper
  used for target selection and backlink validation. Keep the original
  comparison and missing-path behavior so absent or inaccessible checkouts
  can still be unregistered. Add a Windows regression that registers a
  worktree with Git and removes it via its canonical path, and document
  equivalent path selection.
- don't apply the caller's `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or `GIT_WORK_TREE` to a new clone
- preserve caller locations in native error adapters

  <!-- agent -->

  Passing a `#[track_caller]` constructor directly to `map_err()` records
  the `FnOnce` shim in `core` as the caller. Use `or_error()` for native
  error adapters in `gix`, `gix-actor`, and `gix-config` so diagnostics record
  the adapter and use the usual exception formatting, including with
  `tree-error`.

  Keep `Error::from_boxed()` inside a closure for boxed trait-object errors,
  which `ResultExt` does not accept. Add a regression for invalid branch
  merge references and document when constructors still require closures.
- anchor worktree removal paths to the repository CWD

  <!-- agent -->

  A repository opened through a relative path retains the CWD that gives its
  paths meaning. Changing the process CWD before worktree removal made exact
  lookup and suffix disambiguation resolve registrations against the wrong
  location. Registration scans, lock checks, and reopening a selected worktree
  also depended on the process CWD.

  Resolve registered checkout paths with `repo.current_dir()`. Anchor proxy
  private Git directories and reopened common directories to that captured
  CWD, so enumeration, lookup by ID, locks, status, and removal keep using the
  original repository. Keep caller-supplied relative targets relative to the
  current process CWD. Document that proxy paths are now absolute.

  Extend the isolated relative-path removal test with a CWD change and lock
  checks, and cover absolute lookup, ambiguous suffix disambiguation, repository
  inspection, and main-worktree protection from both main and linked handles.
  The new CWD cases failed before the fix.

##### Commit Statistics

- 30 commits contributed to the release over the course of 13 calendar days.
- 13 days passed between releases.
- 11 commits were understood as [conventional](https://www.conventionalcommits.org).
- 2 unique issues were worked on: [#​3039](https://redirect.github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/issues/3039), [#​3040](https://redirect.github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/issues/3040)

pullRequest.title: fix: handle malformed messages missing <|message|> token
pullRequest.body:
StreamableParser now gracefully handles LLM output where stop tokens appear before the expected <|message|> token. The parser extracts header metadata (channel, recipient, content_type) from accumulated tokens and treats the remainder as message content.

Refactors header parsing into a shared helper to eliminate duplication.

pullRequest.title: fix(tests): src-tauri's unit tests start on Windows
pullRequest.body:
### What?

On Windows, `cargo test -p atlas --lib` now starts and runs `src-tauri`'s unit tests. Before, the test executable exited with `0xc0000139, STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND` before running anything.

### Why?

The guess in #332 is right, and I confirmed it on the failing binary:

- The test executable imports `TaskDialogIndirect` from `comctl32.dll` (pulled in by Tauri's dialog code). Only comctl32 **v6** exports it.
- The executable had no `RT_MANIFEST` resource, so Windows bound it to comctl32 v5 and the loader refused to start the process.

tauri-build does embed the manifest, but through the app's resource file, which is linked with `cargo:rustc-link-arg-bins`. That reaches `[[bin]]` targets only, so `atlas.exe` got a manifest and the `--lib` test executable did not.

### How?

`src-tauri/build.rs`, on `windows` + `msvc` only:

- Embed the manifest with the linker for every target the package links: `cargo:rustc-link-arg=/MANIFEST:EMBED` and `/MANIFESTINPUT:<src-tauri/windows-app-manifest.xml>`.
- Build with `WindowsAttributes::new_without_app_manifest()`, so tauri-build does not add a second copy to the app's resource file.

`windows-app-manifest.xml` has the same content as tauri-build's default manifest (the Common-Controls v6 dependency), so `atlas.exe` ends up with the same manifest it had before, just embedded by a different route. macOS, Linux and `windows-gnu` builds take the old path unchanged.

Two things I tried first, in case they come up in review:

- `cargo:rustc-link-arg-tests` is rejected for this package (`does not have a test target`). It covers integration tests, not the unit-test executable.
- `cargo:rustc-link-arg` on its own, keeping tauri-build's manifest, makes the unit tests run but breaks the app link: `CVTRES : fatal error CVT1100: duplicate resource. type:MANIFEST`. That is why the two changes go together.

### Verification (Windows 11, MSVC, Rust 1.99.0, on top of `0.4.1`)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo test -p atlas --lib` | exits `0xc0000139` before any test | 1011 tests run: 991 passed, 14 failed, 6 ignored |
| manifest in the test executable | none | one, Common-Controls v6 |
| `cargo build -p atlas --bin atlas` | links | links |
| manifest in `atlas.exe` | (not inspected) | exactly one, Common-Controls v6 |

I also started the built `atlas.exe` and it came up normally (it logged its agent host, memory server and notifier start-up). I did not use the UI beyond that, and the frontend was a stub `dist/`, so I have left the third checklist box unticked.

**The 14 failures are real Windows failures that were hidden because the binary never started.** They are not caused by this change and I have not touched them here:

- 12 in `commands::skills` (symlink handling)
- 1 in `state::atlas_config` (`an_absolute_xdg_config_home_wins`: `/elsewhere/cfg` is not an absolute path on Windows)
- 1 in `commands::save_guard` (`ordinary_save_targets_pass`)

I can open a follow-up issue listing them if that is useful.

Not run: `bun run ci:local` and the frontend checks; this PR only touches `src-tauri/build.rs` and adds the manifest file. `cargo clippy -p atlas --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops on Windows at an existing lint in `vendor/atlas-engine/utils/path-uri` (`chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size), with or without this change; plain `cargo clippy -p atlas --lib` reports nothing for `build.rs`. I could not test macOS or Linux; the new code returns early there.

Fixes #332

## Checklist

- [x] Targets the current version branch, unless it's a small standalone fix
- [ ] New behaviour has a test; a bug fix has a test that fails without it — there is no test to add for "the test binary starts"; the evidence is the before/after table above.
- [ ] You've run the app and used the change in a window — started it only, see above.

pullRequest.title: test: wait for other snapshots before the `VACUUM` in `join_hot_update_vacuum`
pullRequest.body:
## Ticket(s) Closed

None.

## What

This PR makes `join_hot_update_vacuum` wait for other snapshots before its `VACUUM`.

## Why

The test asserts that `VACUUM` left the page all-visible and the HOT roots redirected. Both come back `f` when another backend holds a snapshot older than the update. `pg_regress` runs one test at a time, so the holder is a background process. The merger keeps a snapshot for its whole merge (`BackgroundWorker::transaction`), and one left by an earlier test is enough. Seen once on #6886 (PG18, `pgrx`, arm64), with the other five matrix jobs green on the same commit.

That snapshot also holds back the vacuum horizon for the whole database while a merge runs, which may be worth a look on its own.

## How

A `DO` block polls `pg_stat_activity` for other backends in this database with a `backend_xmin`. It gives up after 2 minutes with a `WARNING` naming the holders.

## Tests

Reproduced locally with a `REPEATABLE READ` session held open while `pg_regress` ran the test. `main` fails with the CI diff. With this change the test waits out the holder and passes.

pullRequest.title: Fix gamut mapping binary search
pullRequest.body:
Fixes #1298.

The gamut mapping binary search returned as soon as it found a chroma under the JND. The spec keeps searching upward from that point and returns the largest chroma still under the JND. Because of the early return, sRGB fallbacks for wide gamut colors came out less saturated than the spec and colorjs.io produce.

This change follows the spec pseudocode: it clips the origin color once before the loop, carries the `min_inGamut` flag, and returns the last clipped color. The epsilon now matches the spec value and the spec link points to the current anchor.

The same search is implemented in [colordx](https://github.com/dkryaklin/colordx), where it matches colorjs.io on a large set of out of gamut samples. The loop here mirrors that math.

Test expectations that depended on the old behavior are updated, and the cases from the issue are added. All new values match colorjs.io with `method: "css"`.
