pullRequest.title: fix(zerocode): save sidebar changes while another reader has the config open
pullRequest.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode has two writers for its config file. Theme, locale, keybinding, and Config-pane edits go through `secure_file::write_private_atomic`, which stages an owner-only sibling and publishes it with `std::fs::rename`. Sidebar and dock changes (show or hide a section, switch side, resize) went through a separate `write_document_atomically`. That writer staged a `tempfile` and published it with `persist`.
  - On Windows `persist` is a bare `MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`, which fails with `Access is denied. (os error 5)` whenever any reader has the target open, even one that shares delete access. Every zerocode window reads the same config file without a lock, at startup, at session boundaries, and in the Config pane. A dock toggle or resize that overlapped another window's read failed to save and showed the save-failed notice.
  - `persist_sidebar_leaf` now publishes through `write_private_atomic`, the funnel every other config write already uses, and the separate writer is gone. On Windows, `std::fs::rename` retries an access-denied `MoveFileExW` with `SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx)` using `FILE_RENAME_FLAG_POSIX_SEMANTICS`. That moves the name to the new file while open readers keep reading the old one, which is the Unix behavior. On Unix both paths are `rename(2)`.
  - `write_private_atomic`'s doc comment now records why it must use `std::fs::rename` and not `persist`. Its staging file is created with `create_new` and no Windows temporary attribute, so nothing else changes for it.
  - A new test, `sidebar_leaf_write_replaces_a_config_a_reader_holds_open`, saves a sidebar change while a reader holds the config open.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to what the sidebar save writes: the `toml_edit` in-place edit, comment and unknown-key preservation, malformed-section refusal, and environment-shadow reporting are untouched. The sidebar path now also gets the funnel's directory fsync and `0700` directory tightening on Unix, which every other config write already applies. One edge also moves with it: with an explicit empty `--config-dir ""`, the funnel's directory fsync fails after publishing, as it already does for theme and locale saves; the old sidebar writer mapped that empty parent to `.`. No `Cargo.toml` change; `zerocode` still has no `zeroclaw` dependency.
- **Blast radius:** Sidebar and dock persistence in zerocode. Unix behavior is a rename of an owner-only staged file, as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed; no issue tracks this. Related: #11398 and #11400 apply the same fix at the other affected sites. #11362 covers the SOP save fix for the same failure caught by the advisory Windows job.
- **Labels:** `risk:medium`, `zerocode`, `size:XS`, `ci:windows`.

### What this does, simply

zerocode remembers your sidebar layout in its config file. It saves a change by writing a complete new copy and swapping it in for the old file in one step, so nothing ever reads half a file. Other zerocode windows read that same file without waiting. On Windows, the sidebar's swap was done in a way the system refuses whenever anything is reading the file at that moment, so toggling or resizing the sidebar could fail to save because another window was loading the config. Sidebar saves now use the same writer as every other zerocode setting, which swaps the file in a way Windows allows while it is open. A reader that already has the file keeps the old copy, and the next read gets the new one, the same as on Linux and macOS.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on Windows only; Unix already allows replacing an open file.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** zerocode's config persistence (`config::persist_sidebar_width` through `persist_sidebar_leaf`) in unit tests. No `surface` or `channel` value applies.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Windows machine with the MSVC toolchain, or the `ci:windows` label on this PR.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo nextest run -p zerocode --bin zerocode config::tests::sidebar_leaf_write_replaces_a_config_a_reader_holds_open`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Passes. The held handle still reads the old config, and a fresh load sees the new width.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The test does not exist on `master`. Expected, not observed: the same steps against `master`'s sidebar writer fail with `replacing ...: Access is denied. (os error 5)`. That is the same `persist` call the advisory Windows job caught failing for SOP saves in [run 36796530916](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36796530916/job/110161368722).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required Format, Lint, and Test jobs build and run the zerocode tests on Linux, including the new one and the existing sidebar and `secure_file` tests. The advisory Windows job that this PR opts into is the Windows evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows runs only in the opt-in advisory job, and I could not build for Windows locally (`ring`'s build script needs the MSVC and Windows SDK headers). On Unix the new test passes with or without the fix, so only the Windows job can show the before/after difference. That job always runs the hardware step, which fails on Windows until the sibling hardware fix merges; read it for the zerocode results.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  On macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64, rustc 1.97.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.140), at `3e8f4cc8fc` (this branch's head):

  ```text
  $ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 8.95s
  (exit 0)

  $ cargo nextest run --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast
          PASS [   0.091s] ( 765/1451) zerocode::bin/zerocode config::tests::sidebar_leaf_write_replaces_a_config_a_reader_holds_open
          LEAK [   0.342s] ( 888/1451) zerocode::bin/zerocode connection_tests::spawned_daemon_exit_does_not_wait_for_inherited_stderr
       Summary [   7.458s] 1451 tests run: 1451 passed (1 leaky), 2 skipped
  (the leaky test deliberately leaves a child holding stderr)

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh apps/zerocode/src/config/mod.rs apps/zerocode/src/secure_file.rs

The job failed later in four unrelated `zeroclaw-hardware` Arduino upload tests.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Read the implementations this relies on. `tempfile` 3.27.0 `file/imp/windows.rs` `persist` is `MoveFileExW` with no fallback. Rust's `library/std/src/sys/fs/windows.rs` `rename` retries `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` with `FileRenameInfoEx` plus `FILE_RENAME_FLAG_REPLACE_IF_EXISTS | FILE_RENAME_FLAG_POSIX_SEMANTICS`, and std's default share mode includes `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`. zerocode's config readers are std reads.
  - The existing sidebar tests still pass: comments and unknown keys survive, a malformed or non-table `[sidebar]` is refused and left as it was, and environment shadowing is still reported.

  - Not verified locally: the Windows run itself (see the gap above).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`; no user-visible interface state changed. The save-failed notice text and when it appears are unchanged apart from no longer firing for this cause.

pullRequest.title: fix(providers): detect unified llama executable
pullRequest.body:
## Problem

With llama.cpp 0.5.0 installed as the unified `llama` executable, llmfit does not currently discover the provider or select its runtime mode. This behavior is reported in #1097.

## Change

Detect the unified executable when `--help` lists both `cli` and `serve`, expose it as llama.cpp, and prepend the matching subcommand in `llmfit run`. Existing `llama-cli` and `llama-server` paths remain supported.

## Validation

- `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.0 make test` (973 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored)
- `cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all --check`
- `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.0 make clippy` did not pass: 19 diagnostics were reported in unchanged baseline code.
- Detection tests use synthetic help output; a real llama.cpp binary was not available.

## Known limitation

The two-second probe timeout bounds the direct child, but a descendant that inherits stdout or stderr can keep the reader join waiting indefinitely after the child exits. The existing timeout test does not cover this case.

Fixes #1097

pullRequest.title: 完善skill管理界面
pullRequest.body:
做了一个完整的skill管理界面，基础功能基本都有吧

本地已安装的 Skill 原先未正确出现在“已安装”中，仍显示安装入口；仓库添加、编辑和目录刷新也缺少完整反馈。仓库扫描期间会禁用切换操作，大目录一次挂载全部条目，打开 Skill 详情还会退出仓库管理。

本 PR 完善同一套 Skills 管理流程：

- 正确识别本地已安装状态，支持临时启停、从 cc-switch 导入，以及更新时保留停用状态。
- 展示已添加仓库，支持链接解析、编辑、启停和删除；保存前检查可访问性并扫描 Skill，验证失败不保存。递归发现根目录与嵌套目录中的 `SKILL.md`，修正同名条目冲突，并持久化仓库目录缓存。
- GitHub API 失败时支持 codeload ZIP 回退，识别默认分支，并对 GitHub 目标地址解析 Windows 自动代理。
- 仓库管理占满窗口，压缩侧栏行高，增强深色分割线和文字层级；添加、编辑面板固定在底部，详情与安装状态保持列对齐。
- 浏览操作不再受扫描锁影响，过期扫描响应不会覆盖当前选择；列表仅挂载可视区域附近的条目。详情叠加打开，关闭后保留仓库选择、搜索词和滚动位置，Escape 只关闭最上层面板。
- 卸载前备份本地实体目录与受控源，保留复制回退后的用户修改；备份失败不直接删除唯一副本。cc-switch 同名导入先暂存，保留冲突内容，切换或状态保存失败时回滚。
- 远端 Skill 使用稳定的仓库路径身份，安装记录保存来源路径；新增同名目录不会转移安装状态或更新目标。缺少路径的旧安装记录继续保留，但拒绝不确定的自动覆盖，需要先备份卸载再重新安装。
- 已保存仓库仅变更启停状态时本地保存，不依赖仓库可访问性；新增或修改地址、分支、子目录仍须验证后保存。无变更的保存仍执行验证和扫描。
- 复制安装的 Skill 停用时先暂存当前内容，保留用户修改和来源信息；本地接管拒绝将源目录放入待复制目录内部。停用和卸载在状态保存失败或中途备份失败时恢复原目录与记录，提交后的备份清理失败不误报为事务失败。
- 备份恢复先暂存内容，再一起提交目录、启用链接和记录；保存或建链失败仍保留原备份。恢复遇到已存在的源或本地目录时拒绝覆盖；启用也不会删除缺少清单的现有目录，复制启用失败会清理半成品。

验证：

- 独立 PR 分支：TypeScript 检查、前端测试（625 通过、1 跳过）、Vite 生产构建和 `cargo check -p codex-plus-manager --tests --locked` 通过；差异检查通过。
- 相同 Skills 实现已在隔离的 Windows 管理器中验证真实仓库扫描、解析保存、安装、缓存恢复和布局。挂起首次加载时仍能切换仓库；864 项目录只挂载可视区条目且可滚动到底；详情关闭后选择、搜索和滚动位置保持不变。可用 `node scripts/test-skills-repository-browser.mjs <release-executable>` 复验。
- 独立分支的 Rust Skills 测试在链接阶段受现有 `sherpa-onnx` 静态库与 MSVC 标准库符号不兼容阻挡（LNK2019/LNK1120），未将该次测试记为通过。本 PR 不修改相关音频依赖的链接配置。
- 当前 Skills 核心回归 43 项、生命周期专项回归 10 项通过，覆盖本地唯一副本恢复、不同实体副本保留、备份失败、导入冲突和保存失败回滚、同名路径新增、旧记录拒绝误更新、不可访问仓库的本地启停，以及复制安装保留修改、只读状态文件回滚、Windows 目录占用、递归暂存保护、恢复保存或建链失败和本地目录冲突保护。该运行使用共享音频库的本地构建配置；独立 PR 分支保持原有依赖配置，双平台完整验证以新 head CI 为准。
- 新 Release 已通过隔离原生管理器回归，包含本地 Skill 卸载恢复原文、只读状态下恢复失败仍保留备份、恢复拒绝覆盖本地内容、停用再启用保留修改、只读状态文件下停用和卸载失败恢复、外部目录联接接管、不可访问仓库直接停用，以及既有仓库扫描、安装、嵌套详情、窄窗口、无底部冗余栏和列表响应性检查；测试实例和状态已清理。最新独立 PR 分支的生命周期测试 `cargo check` 通过。

pullRequest.title: Fix `copy_prop_reverse` cycle detection
pullRequest.body:
## Description

This PR solves a bug when a valid `sway` code generates a cycle of `memcpys`. One simple example is the `e2e` test at `test/src/e2e_vm_tests/test_programs/should_pass/language/references/arg_ref_mut_return_by_value`.

The IR generated is something like:

```
v35v1 = get_local __ptr { u64 }, s, !30
...
v76v1 = load v35v1, !33
br block0(v76v1), !33

block0(mut v71v1: { u64 }):
v38v1 = get_local __ptr { u64 }, s, !41
store v71v1 to v38v1, !41
```

We end-up copying `s` into itself. 

The issue that this caused was that `copy_prop_reverse` inside the `memcpyopt` was hanging forever. 

Now, `copy_prop_reverse` cycle detection is more robust and detect any cycle, but we just bail all the optimizations as before.

To mark future improvements, I have add some optimizations I found at https://github.com/FuelLabs/sway/issues/7282#issuecomment-5196527165, and have put some TODOS around the code pointing to this issue.

pullRequest.title: Improve no repeat priority
pullRequest.body:
Closes #2266

This seems like a rather trivial issue. Priority for mappings is determined by a) the number of modifiers then b) the order in declaration. When a key is initially pressed, it is necessary to match the highest priority action from both the repeat and non repeat list. This mandates that the lists are combined into one `KeyMappingEntries` for all key down events to preserve the ordering.

If the matched action is a KeyDownNoRepeat but the event is just a KeyDown then it is simply a noop. I do not think it would be useful to fall back in this case.

The fix benefits the path tool where it is now possible to use <kbd>tab</kbd> while dragging a handle to switch to the next handle again (previously it would change to the select tool).

I have not updated any of the input definitions as it seems it would be a bit subjective.

pullRequest.title: Add chained filter sections
pullRequest.body:
Adds support for chaining multiple filters in a single `{% filter %} ... {% endfilter %}` section, with each filter delimited by the `|` character. For instance, the following:

```jinja2
{% filter safe %}{% filter replace(from="Robert", to="Bob") %}{% filter indent %}
Hello, I'm Robert!
{% endfilter %}{% endfilter %}{% endfilter %}
```

may now be rewritten as:

```jinja2
{% filter indent | replace(from="Robert", to="Bob") | safe %}
Hello, I'm Robert!
{% endfilter %}
```

Closes #757.

Looking forward to using this feature while tackling https://github.com/ebkalderon/terminus/issues/27.

pullRequest.title: fix: Windows 端串流后音量环动画持续卡顿（clip-path 回收至 Linux，串流循环动画改 CSS）
pullRequest.body:
## 为什么改

v2.1.0 在 Windows 实机上：启动后首次连接进入串流，主界面音量环动画出现不间断卡顿，像被反复短暂阻塞；空闲时不卡，一串流就卡。

此前怀疑过 DSP/ONNX 模型首包加载阻塞音频线程，做过「模型预热 + 陈旧积压丢弃」并在实机验证——症状无任何变化，已回滚，后端方向排除。

排查 2.1.0 前端改动后定位到两个回归点，都恰好只在串流期间持续生效：

1. **全局 `body { clip-path: inset(0 round 1rem) }`**（#353 引入）。#353 的圆角设计是分平台的：「Windows DWM 圆角偏好、macOS vibrancy、Linux clip-path」，但实现落在了全局 CSS，Windows/macOS 也被无差别裁剪。Chromium/WebView2 里文档级圆角裁剪让整页内容每帧都要经过带遮罩的合成表面；主窗口本身是透明 + acrylic 的重合成路径，串流时音量环每帧 rAF 写 SVG 属性、辉光/脉冲每帧弄脏页面，叠加每帧全窗口遮罩合成后持续掉帧——就是「不间断卡顿」的直接来源。该裁剪在 Windows 上冗余：Win11 有 DWM 圆角裁剪，Win10 回到 v2.0.3 的内容自绘圆角观感。

2. **anime.js v3→v4 后，两个无限循环动画跑在主线程**（中央辉光呼吸 2s、底栏状态点脉冲 1.5s，均仅 streaming 状态运行）。v4 引擎每帧在主线程 tick 并写内联样式，与 ~8Hz 的 audio-level IPC 事件、Vue 重渲染、音量环自身的 rAF 循环争抢主线程，在被 ① 拖慢的合成路径上进一步放大掉帧。

已排除的方向（均有代码/实测证据）：`AudioRing.vue` 两版无 diff；level/metrics 事件频率两版一致；jitter prebuffer 时间制只影响起播；`queued_ms` 已由 8f3c4c3 改为原子读；anime.js 上游帧率缺陷（juliangarnier/anime#1112）在 4.3.0 已修复、本仓库锁定 4.5.0；`windowEffects` 配置两版相同；`useWindowEffects` 在非 Linux 平台一次性闩锁、无持续开销。

## 改了什么

纯前端（CSS/Vue），后端零改动，未 bump 版本：

- `src/shared/assets/index.css`
  - `body` 的 clip-path 移入 `.platform-linux body`（App/设置窗口挂载时已由 `applyPlatformClasses()` 打类，Linux 行为不变；Windows 交还 DWM 圆角、macOS 交还 vibrancy）
  - 新增 `glow-breathe` / `dot-pulse` keyframes 与工具类：仅 transform/opacity，由合成器驱动，时长与缓动同原 anime 参数（2s inOutSine alternate / 1.5s inOutQuad），并自动被现有 `prefers-reduced-motion` 规则覆盖（原 anime 循环不理会该设置）
- `src/App.vue`：删除两个 anime.js 循环动画的 `watchEffect` 与相关 ref/变量，模板改用上述 CSS 类（辉光元素本身仅 streaming 挂载；状态点按状态绑定 `dot-pulse`）；anime.js 保留用于一次性交互（悬停、点击回弹）；清理未用导入（`watchEffect`/`utils`/`JSAnimation`）
- `src/features/plugins/components/PluginPanelWindow.vue`：插件面板窗口根容器补 `rounded-2xl`——该窗口不调用 `applyPlatformClasses`，原先依赖文档级 clip 获得圆角，现在自绘（视觉上与原先一致，同为 1rem 圆角）
- `AGENTS.md`：记录平台化圆角策略与「持续动画走合成器 CSS 动画、JS 动画库仅用于一次性交互」的约定

## 验证

- **Windows 实机**（原症状复现环境）：安装本分支 CI 构建包复测，首次连接串流下音量环动画平滑，卡顿消失
- Linux 不受影响：clip-path 在 `.platform-linux` 下原样保留，KDE Wayland 原生模糊/阴影逻辑未动

pullRequest.title: fix(block): require light level 9 for crop growth
pullRequest.body: ## Description > This description was drafted by an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). Fixes the remaining part of #3516. Stems got the light check in #4013, but `CropBlockBase::random_tick` still grew wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots and torchflowers in complete darkness. Vanilla `CropBlock.randomTick` (26.3) only grows when `level.getRawBrightness(pos, 0) >= 9`. The check now runs first in `CropBlockBase::random_tick`, same as `StemBlock`. The `9` is shared as `MIN_GROWTH_LIGHT`, so stems use the same constant instead of a bare number. Callers: wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots and torchflowers go through this path, and all of them extend `CropBlock` in vanilla. Sweet berry bush and nether wart override `random_tick` and are unaffected. Bone meal is unchanged. Noticed but left out of this PR: - Sky light isn't lowered when blocks are placed around an already sky-lit spot. A wheat crop inside a closed stone box made with `/fill` in open air still reads sky light 15, so it keeps growing. Crops underground read 0 as expected. - Beetroot grows on `random_range(0..3) == 0` (1/3) and torchflower on `random_range(0..2) != 0` (1/2), while vanilla uses `nextInt(3) != 0` (2/3) for both. - Vanilla `CropBlock.canSurvive` also requires raw brightness >= 8. Pumpkin doesn't check that yet. - `/forceload add` marks a chunk as forced but doesn't load it when no player is nearby. ## Testing - Checked against decompiled 26.3 `CropBlock`, `StemBlock`, `BeetrootBlock` and `TorchflowerCropBlock`. - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pumpkin-core --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo test -p pumpkin-core` pass. - Ran the same scenario on `master` and on this branch with a headless client and `random_tick_speed 300`. Wheat and carrots were placed in a sealed room 40 blocks underground (raw brightness 0) and on the surface (raw brightness 15). Over about 80 seconds: - `master`: the underground wheat and carrots grew to age 4. - This branch: the underground crops stayed at age 0 after about 50 random ticks each, and the surface crops grew normally. - Same check on this branch with water next to both plots and `random_tick_speed 200`: the surface wheat reached age 7 in about a minute, while the underground wheat stayed at age 0 on moist farmland for five minutes. - In-game with a real client, on one farmland plot with water: the wheat under open sky (client light 15) reached `age: 7`, while the wheat in the closed-off part of the same plot (client light 0) stayed at `age: 0`. Capture: ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Crop growth now consistently requires a minimum light level of 9. Crops below this threshold won’t advance in age, and gourd stems follow the same light requirement. Existing growth and moisture checks continue when the light level is sufficient.

pullRequest.title: [MOD-17680] Fix crashes in CONTAINS and suffix TAG queries on macOS x86_64
pullRequest.body:
## Describe the changes in the pull request

1. Current: The Rust global allocator returns memory aligned only to 16 bytes, whatever alignment a type asks for. The Redis module allocator has no aligned-allocation call. On macOS x86_64, the AVX2 substring searcher behind CONTAINS and suffix TAG queries needs 32 bytes, so it gets misaligned memory. That is undefined behavior: assertion-enabled builds abort with `misaligned pointer dereference`, and release builds are exposed to crashes or silent corruption. Linux is masked by jemalloc's size classes and aarch64 by a 16-byte NEON searcher, by accident rather than by guarantee.
2. Change: Allocations that need more than 16-byte alignment get a correctly aligned block. Allocations needing 16 bytes or less, which is nearly all of them, go to the Redis allocator exactly as before.
3. Outcome: CONTAINS, suffix and wildcard TAG queries no longer crash on macOS x86_64. A future dependency bump or a new over-aligned type can no longer bring the bug back on other platforms.

#### Which additional issues this PR fixes

1. [MOD-17680](https://redislabs.atlassian.net/browse/MOD-17680)

#### Main objects this PR modified

1. New `over_aligned_alloc` crate. Its `OverAligned` adapter serves an over-aligned layout from an inner block padded by the alignment, and keeps the inner block's address just below the returned pointer for deallocation.
2. `redisearch_rs` registers `OverAligned<RedisAlloc>` as the global allocator.

**Review focus:** the pointer arithmetic in `OverAligned::place`, and the `realloc` path for over-aligned blocks, which copies into a new block. The tests drive the adapter over an inner allocator whose addresses are always 16-byte but never 32-byte aligned, so the failure is deterministic on every machine, and they pass under Miri.

**Memory:** an over-aligned allocation costs `align` extra bytes, all of it counted by Redis's allocator. Only a few types are over-aligned (today the AVX2 searcher, one per CONTAINS iterator), so the cost is negligible.

**Manual validation:** PR CI does not run on macOS, so I dispatched macOS x86_64 flow tests by hand. Results will follow in a comment.

#### Mark if applicable

- [ ] This PR introduces API changes
- [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes

#### Release Notes

- [x] This PR requires release notes
- [ ] This PR does not require release notes

If a release note is required (bug fix / new feature / enhancement), describe the **user impact** of this PR in the title.

pullRequest.title: Fix optional OpenSSL duplex I/O on Unix
pullRequest.body:
# Fix optional OpenSSL duplex I/O on Unix

Follow-up to #9167. A blocking read currently holds the connection lock while waiting for network input, preventing a concurrent write on the same TLS connection from making progress.

This change removes that deadlock on Unix platforms with `MSG_DONTWAIT`, without changing the shared socket's blocking flags. Windows and AIX retain the legacy transport and its blocking-I/O limitation. Linux and macOS optional OpenSSL runtime validation passed in hosted CI; the local results below are Linux only.

## Implementation

- Serialize each native SSL attempt, error inspection and callback snapshot, then release the connection lock before waiting for socket readiness.
- Preserve OpenSSL's write-retry contract with stable owned pending bytes and explicit retry ownership. `WANT_WRITE` prevents conflicting native calls; `WANT_READ` permits safe read progress.
- Register anonymous-pipe wakeups before unlocking, and notify waiters on native progress, ownership changes and socket invalidation.
- Allocate socket identity tracking lazily for SSL. Close, detach and reinitialization wake waiters; each native transport call validates identity to reject descriptor reuse. Reinitialization unlocks and notifies before dropping the old native socket.
- Settle write ownership and capture owned callback/native-error metadata under the SSL guard, then construct Python exceptions after unlocking. Preserve certificate-verification metadata when a debug callback also fails.
- Extend the existing SSL snippet for buffer-export release, writer-return/reader-callback cleanup, and an explicitly reached application `WANT_WRITE` followed by valid saved-byte retry and exact delivery/EOF. Positive partial writes are supported.
- Extend the existing OpenSSL build step with the shared snippet and full canonical SSL suite on Linux/macOS, preserving the minimal-feature and vendored build checks. Canonical `Lib/test/test_ssl.py` remains untouched, with no new exclusion or weakened assertion.

A timed-out, interrupted or nonblocking write can retain a native continuation. Retry with the same bytes and length. Until an abandoned `WANT_WRITE` continuation is retried, conflicting I/O reports `SSLWantWriteError` instead of making a forbidden native call. Close/detach remain escape routes; equal concurrent writes are still distinct calls.

This addresses the lock held across a read-readiness wait. Strict OpenSSL `WANT_WRITE` ownership does not guarantee liveness under arbitrary two-peer backpressure. Acquiring the native lock behind a long-running Python callback is not newly deadline-aware.

## Validation

Locally on the final tree rebased onto `fc9f4a9` (native tests/checks use their normal Cargo profiles; interpreter runtime checks use fresh release binaries):

- 14 native retry-ownership, progress-waiter and socket-identity tests passed.
- Threaded/nonthreaded OpenSSL checks and the OpenSSL 1.1.1w compile-only floor check passed.
- Full unchanged `test_ssl`: OpenSSL **215 total / 189 executed passes / 26 skips**; default rustls **215 total / 175 executed passes / 40 skips**.
- Canonical callback-exception/duplex selectors: **2 passes**.
- Exact final snippet passed on CPython 3.15 first, then OpenSSL and rustls; the existing focused pytest harness also passed once per RustPython backend.
- Normal repository hooks passed. Optional OpenSSL Clippy still fails with **41 inherited diagnostics**; comparison against the earlier log confirms the introduced findings were removed.

Additional completed evidence before the importlib rebase and mechanical lint cleanup: workspace native **1,369 passes**; separate ABI3T C-API **123 passes / 4 ignores**; workspace docs **24 passes / 18 ignores**; C-API docs had no cases. Workspace and separate C-API Clippy passed. The production retry/wakeup implementation was unchanged by that cleanup.

That earlier source also passed 20 TLS 1.3 and 20 TLS 1.2-bound invocations of the canonical duplex method, plus CPython-first timeout/callback and certificate-metadata checks. These are bounded scheduling/compatibility checks, not exhaustive stress or fuzz coverage. Existing resource/platform skips remain. Broad local `test_socket` was not run; socket evidence consists of native identity tests and canonical SSL lifecycle coverage.

[Main hosted CI](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/actions/runs/39036742789) passed all 25 jobs at `0617d622`, including actionlint and the mandatory zizmor scan. The optional OpenSSL build, shared snippet and unchanged full SSL suite passed on both Linux (OpenSSL 3.0.13) and macOS (OpenSSL 4.0.3). Each hosted SSL run reported **215 total / 186 executed passes / 29 skips**, with the canonical duplex and callback-exception methods executed successfully. Windows default-backend CI passed; optional OpenSSL runtime steps were intentionally not run there. The consolidated Linux/macOS Rust jobs finished in 29m32s and 26m50s, within the unchanged 45-minute job limit.

The separate [CodSpeed run](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/actions/runs/39036742733) failed during its build with exit code 143 before any benchmarks executed. No Rust diagnostic was reported; a maintainer rerun is needed. This remains a failed check, separate from the successful main CI.

Windows needs a separately agreed transport compatibility contract. The existing trailing-`None` SSL exception `args` mismatch and rustls callback-settlement follow-ups are outside this change.

## AI assistance

Implementation, test preparation and review were assisted by OpenAI Codex (model version unavailable).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved TLS socket handling on Unix, including nonblocking I/O, timeouts, interruption handling, and connection-close notifications.
  * Made concurrent TLS reads and writes more reliable by preserving pending write data and enforcing correct retries.
  * Improved certificate-verification error reporting across platforms.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for TLS write retries, concurrent socket activity, and bounded echo-server behavior.
  * Expanded OpenSSL build and SSL test coverage across non-Windows platforms.

## Summary

**Available models:**
| Model | Context | Max Output |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` | 164K | 65K |

| `z-ai/glm-5` | 131K | 16K |
| `minimax/minimax-m2.5` | 1M | 1M |

**Example configuration:**
```toml
[model.chat.http]
kind = "avian/chat"
model_name = "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2"
api_endpoint = "https://api.avian.io/v1"
api_key = "your-api-key"
```

## Changes

- `crates/http-api-bindings/src/chat/mod.rs` — Add `"avian/chat"` to the match arm for OpenAI-compatible chat providers
- `website/docs/references/models-http-api/avian.md` — Documentation page with setup instructions

pullRequest.title: Show unchanged lines that fall inside an inline hunk
pullRequest.body:
Closes #978.

## Bug

When two novel lines in a hunk are close enough that the merge step in `display::hunks::merge_adjacent` combines them into one hunk, the unchanged lines between them are silently dropped from inline (`--display=inline`) output. Side-by-side and JSON output don't have this problem because both use `matched_lines_indexes_for_hunk` to walk the full hunk range, so they already include the in-between unchanged lines. Inline was iterating `hunk.lines` directly, and that field only contains positions with novel content.

In the report this surfaces as a missing section heading on a `.gitconfig`:

```
$ difft before.gitconfig after.gitconfig --display=inline
```

The line `[url "ssh://git@github.com"]` between two changed `pushInsteadOf =` lines does not appear.

## Repro

`before.gitconfig`:

```
[uploadpack]
    allowFilter = true

[url "ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org"]
    pushInsteadOf = "https://aur.archlinux.org"

[url "ssh://git@github.com"]
    pushInsteadOf = "https://github.com"

[versionsort]
    # prereleaseSuffix is deprecated in favour of suffix
```

`after.gitconfig` (same, but both `pushInsteadOf` lines are commented out):

```
[uploadpack]
    allowFilter = true

[url "ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org"]
    ; pushInsteadOf = "https://aur.archlinux.org"

[url "ssh://git@github.com"]
    ; pushInsteadOf = "https://github.com"

[versionsort]
    # prereleaseSuffix is deprecated in favour of suffix
```

### Before this PR

```
/tmp/after3.gitconfig --- Text
1    [uploadpack]
2        allowFilter = true
3    
4    [url "ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org"]
5        pushInsteadOf = "https://aur.archlinux.org"
8        pushInsteadOf = "https://github.com"
   5     ; pushInsteadOf = "https://aur.archlinux.org"
   8     ; pushInsteadOf = "https://github.com"
   9 
   10 [versionsort]
   11     # prereleaseSuffix is deprecated in favour of suffix
```

Lines 6 (blank) and 7 (`[url "ssh://git@github.com"]`) are missing on both sides.

### After this PR

```
/tmp/after3.gitconfig --- Text
1    [uploadpack]
2        allowFilter = true
3    
4    [url "ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org"]
5        pushInsteadOf = "https://aur.archlinux.org"
6    
7    [url "ssh://git@github.com"]
8        pushInsteadOf = "https://github.com"
   5     ; pushInsteadOf = "https://aur.archlinux.org"
   6 
   7 [url "ssh://git@github.com"]
   8     ; pushInsteadOf = "https://github.com"
   9 
   10 [versionsort]
   11     # prereleaseSuffix is deprecated in favour of suffix
```

## Fix

Add a small `fill_in_hunk_gaps` helper in `src/display/inline.rs` that walks `hunk.lines` and emits the intervening line numbers for each side, then update the LHS and RHS print loops to consult `hunk.novel_lhs` / `hunk.novel_rhs` so the new gap entries render with dimmed (context) line numbers instead of bold red / green ones.

I considered switching inline to use `all_matched_lines_filled` + `matched_lines_indexes_for_hunk` the same way side-by-side does, but that would also require restructuring how the before / after context loops are integrated. This narrower change keeps the existing structure and only fixes the dropped-context-inside-hunk case.

## Testing

- Added four unit tests for `fill_in_hunk_gaps` covering the empty input, no-gap, LHS-only-changes-with-an-unchanged-tail, and unequal-side-gaps shapes.
- `cargo test --release` (148 tests) passes.
- Manually verified against the `.gitconfig` repro above and against syntactic (Rust) inputs to confirm the multi-hunk path still splits correctly when changes are far apart.

pullRequest.title: feat: add support for --shebang flag

pullRequest.body:
### Issue # (if available)

n/a

### Description of changes

Additional Streams WPT cases exposed several gaps in stream state handling. This PR addresses them by pattern:

- **Readable enqueue after cancellation:** Make internal enqueue a no-op when the stream can no longer accept chunks, while keeping the public TransformStream controller enqueue strict.
- **TransformStream error propagation:** Preserve the readable-side error reason when enqueue fails, and avoid updating backpressure after the readable side has closed or errored.
- **TransformStream cancellation and abort races:** Track in-progress cancel/flush operations and their promises so callbacks are not run or finalized inconsistently. Propagate cancellation errors and ensure pending backpressure operations are settled correctly.
- **pipeTo write scheduling:** Defer destination writes so the read/write promise state is updated in the correct order.
- **Streams API typings:** Align `stream/web` declarations with supported APIs, including TransformStream, BYOB read options, and `WritableStreamDefaultController.signal`.

pullRequest.body: I hereby agree to the terms of the CLA available at: https://docs.databend.com/dev/policies/cla/ ## Summary Add `send_notification` as the Query SQL entry point for explicitly sending a notification through an existing notification integration: ```sql CALL system$send_notification('oncall', 'Query errors detected'); SELECT * FROM send_notification('oncall', 'Query errors detected'); ``` - Align the notification protobuf contract with CloudControl's asynchronous enqueue API, including `query_id`, `delivery_id`, and history correlation/filter fields. - Execute one enqueue RPC when the local table-function source runs, not when the function is bound or planned. Disable query-result caching for queries using this function. - Require global `SUPER` privilege for the actual system table function and validate the two string arguments, including the 1–262,144 UTF-8 byte message limit. Ordinary tables named `send_notification` (or another registered function) retain normal table-grant checks; factory name registration alone does not identify their object type. - Use the normal `CALL system$...` rewrite to a table function without notification-specific result suppression. Both `CALL` and `SELECT` expose a `result STRING` column and return zero rows (`has_result_set = true`); no delivery ID or status row is returned. RPC errors still fail SQL. - Propagate enqueue errors to SQL, explicitly report unsupported older CloudControl servers, and do not automatically retry the RPC. A business rejection carried in `EnqueueNotificationResponse.error` is reported as the new `CloudControlNotificationRejected` (1704) instead of `Internal`, since it is not a Databend bug. Errors that CloudControl returns as a gRPC status keep the existing generic status conversion. - Consolidate notification acceptance/errors, no-retry, argument-validation, planning/execution, cache, and privilege regressions in the existing SQL and shell suites. No standalone Query/client test module, Python mock unittest file, or notification guide is added. Success means that CloudControl has persisted the delivery, not that the webhook has completed. Query does not call the webhook or render its payload. An asynchronous delivery failure does not change the already-completed SQL result. For conditional sends or script variables, use the table-function statement in script control flow: ```sql EXECUTE IMMEDIATE $$ BEGIN LET message := 'Query errors detected'; IF TRUE THEN SELECT * FROM send_notification('oncall', :message); END IF; END; $$; ``` ## Compatibility and rollout - The SQL entry point is `send_notification` / `CALL system$send_notification`. Existing tenant UDF/UDTF lookup precedence is unchanged. There are no preflight name-collision checks, name reservations, or automatic migrations; users resolve same-name collisions by renaming their functions. - **Behavior tightening for same-named ordinary tables.** Before this PR, a permanent table whose name matched any registered table function (for example `numbers`) skipped table-level privilege checks entirely; those restricted to `SUPER` (`fuse_amend`, `set_cache_capacity`) instead required `SUPER`. Such tables now follow normal table grants. Users who were relying on the old bypass may now get permission errors and must grant the needed table privileges or rename the table. As with UDF/UDTF collisions, no automatic migration or compatibility shim is provided. - The SQL spelling change is Query-only: `EnqueueNotification`, protobuf messages/field numbers, request metadata, and the CloudControl server/worker implementation are unchanged. No CloudControl rebuild or redeploy is required for changing the SQL name. - Enable the existing `cloud_control_grpc_server_address` configuration and deploy a CloudControl version supporting `EnqueueNotification`. Query fails explicitly against an older server; there is no synchronous fallback. - `query_id` is a correlation key, not an idempotency key. A timeout or lost response can occur after persistence, so manually rerunning the SQL may produce another delivery. - The protobuf query ID remains optional; this Query entry point always supplies the current query ID. The Python mock preserves optional-field presence and distinguishes an absent ID from an explicitly empty ID when filtering history. - This PR does not expose `query_id` in `system.notification_history`; correlation is available through the history RPC. - `CALL` takes literal string arguments. Use the table-function `SELECT` form for expressions or script variables. - The table function is an execution-side effect, not a data-producing relation. Do not use `LIMIT`, filters, or joins to control sending; use script control flow. - Known limitation: a statement that is only planned can still send if `send_notification` appears inside a scalar subquery used as another table function's argument, e.g. `EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM numbers((SELECT count(*) FROM send_notification(...)))`. The binder evaluates such argument subqueries during planning by running a real nested query; this is existing behavior for all table functions (the side-effecting `set_cache_capacity` behaves the same) and is not changed here. A direct `EXPLAIN` / `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` of `send_notification` does not send. ## Tests - [ ] Unit Test - [x] Logic Test - [ ] Benchmark Test - [ ] No Test - _Explain why_ The feature branch was rebased onto upstream `main` commit `af402d7444`. For `send_lost_response`, the mock records every attempt synchronously before always returning `UNAVAILABLE`. SQL must fail with the fixed message, while history must contain exactly one row with the expected payload/source. An automatic retry creates additional rows and fails the assertion; no sleep, randomness, real webhook, or eventual-consistency wait is involved. - Python formatting and shell formatting pass; Ruff reports no newly introduced diagnostics compared with the upstream merge base. Existing generated-protobuf diagnostics and the unrelated mock task variable diagnostic are unchanged. - Before the tenant-isolation fix, the original mock reproduced the CI mismatch in the full parallel task suite. pullRequest.title: add exceptional shift
pullRequest.body:
### Summary of Changes
This PR fixes some cases where the search for eigenvalue could hang. This was solved by using the "Exceptional Shift" method in Wilkinson, J. H., & Reinsch, C. (1971). 
Handbook for automatic computation (Vol. 2: Linear algebra). 

### Details
I first checked why the Lapack algorithm would converge and not hang. I looked at dlahqr procedure (https://netlib.org/lapack/explore-html/d8/df4/group__lahqr_ga100049ab080cef756846702a33e8e28f.html) saw the mention of the exceptional shift and the Ahues & Tisseur stopping criterion.

The last one was a red herring, I implemented it but the test matrix from #611 would still hang. I then implemented the exceptional shift and it worked. I tried tracing back the magical value (0.75 & -0.4375), and discovered https://www.netlib.org/eispack/hqr.f that led me to the original source:

Wilkinson, J. H., & Reinsch, C. (1971). 
Handbook for automatic computation (Vol. 2: Linear algebra).

You can view the orignal magical number and algorithm implementation here : https://www.scribd.com/document/568239788/Wilkinson-Reinsch1971-Book-HandbookForAutomaticComputatio#page=373
 
AI was used to find the original paper

### Testing
I implemented a test with the matrix from #611 that now pass successfully

Fixes #611

SPIR-V uses the first 16 bits of its first word to indicate the instruction's word count. Unfortunately, `Instruction`s count word with `u32`s, and did not check that the `Instruction`'s `wc` actually fit in a `u16` before packing it in. 😳 Eek!

pullRequest.title: Add --worker-threads flag to set the runtime thread count
pullRequest.body:
Add a `--worker-threads` flag to control the number of OS threads the async runtime uses, so the count can be set per invocation without having to export an environment variable.

`oha` already honours `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` when building the Tokio runtime, but there was no way to set it from the command line and it wasn't discoverable from `--help`. This adds a `--worker-threads <N>` option that surfaces the same knob. The flag takes precedence over the environment variable; when neither is set the previous default (the number of physical CPU cores) is unchanged, so existing behaviour is untouched.

Because the runtime is built before the CLI is parsed, `main` now parses `Opts` first and then builds the runtime using the resolved value. The argument is a `NonZeroUsize`, so `0` and negative values are rejected by the parser with a clear error rather than panicking inside Tokio.

Closes #574.

## Testing

- `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt --check`.
- Verified manually: `oha --worker-threads 2 -n 10 --no-tui http://127.0.0.1:PORT/` runs, and `oha --help` lists the new option.

pullRequest.title: fix(http1): synchronize dispatch shutdown with sends
pullRequest.body:
Fixes #4122.

## Summary

- close the HTTP/1 dispatch receiver before teardown
- continue polling the closed receiver until a concurrent synchronous send has either published its envelope or observed the closure
- add a regression test that exercises the close/send race 10,000 times

## Background

Tokio's unbounded channel reserves message capacity before it publishes the
envelope into the channel list. Receiver shutdown could close the channel and
observe a pending receive during that window. The send would then finish after
shutdown, leaving the request owned by the channel until the remaining
`SendRequest` was dropped.

After closing the receiver, `Pending` means that such a pre-close send is still
in flight. Retrying the existing single-poll receive until it yields the
envelope or reports the closed channel removes that window without introducing
an additional synchronization object. The HTTP/2 path remains unchanged.

## Validation

- `cargo test --features full` (309 passed, 10 ignored)
- `cargo +1.97.1 clippy --features full -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check --no-default-features --features client,http1`
- `cargo check --no-default-features --features client,http2`
- `cargo check --no-default-features --features client,http1,http2`
- minimal dependency resolution followed by `cargo check --features full`

pullRequest.title: Fix security vulnerabilities: sanitize ytdlp arguments and prevent XSS in useLinkify
pullRequest.body:
## fix(security): redact sensitive arguments from yt-dlp command logs

### Vulnerability

`ytdlp_runner.rs` was logging the full yt-dlp command line via `tracing::debug!` before execution in both `output()` and `spawn()`:

```rust
tracing::info!("Running command: yt-dlp {}", self.args.join(" "));
```

This exposed credentials in plain text, including:

--username / -u
--password / -p
--video-password
--ap-username / --ap-password (if used)
--proxy (may contain embedded credentials like http://user:pass@host)
--add-header (any header, but especially Authorization:Bearer and Cookie)
--cookies (file path, which may reveal user directory structure)
--extractor-args (can include API keys, e.g. youtube:api_key=...)
--sponsorblock-api (can include a personal API key)

### Impact

Secrets were written to local log files and could be transmitted to Sentry,
an external error-tracking service integrated with the application.
When the app reports an error, Sentry captures recent logs as context and sends
them to its servers, meaning credentials could leave the user's machine
without their knowledge.

**_This change only affects what is written to the logs. The command sent to the yt-dlp subprocess remains exactly the same as before, no functionality is altered_**

### Fix

Added a `sanitize_args_for_log` function that masks sensitive values with `[REDACTED]`
before logging. The actual arguments passed to yt-dlp are not modified.

```rust
// Before (vulnerable)
tracing::debug!("Running command: yt-dlp {}", self.args.join(" "));

// After (safe)
tracing::debug!(
  "Running command: yt-dlp {}",
  sanitize_args_for_log(&self.args)
);
```

### Testing

- Added `sanitize_args_redacts_sensitive_values` unit test that verifies
-- All sensitive flags are correctly masked.
-- The original values never appear in the sanitised output.
-- Non‑sensitive flags (like --url, --no-playlist, etc.) remain untouched.

pullRequest.title: `log-layer-changes-name-only` option
pullRequest.body:
Currently, if `log-layer-changes` is enabled, the *entire* layer definition is printed to your log.
This comes from `deflayer`-based thinking, where a layer can cleanly and helpfully fit on your screen, when you're looking at the log. \
However, if your config is mostly `deflayermap`s, they are often so tall that you don't even *see* the name of the layer.
And then to scroll up to see it you realistically will enter the layer where you have your scrolling hotkeys, further bloating up the output before you can ever encounter the information you were looking for to begin with. \
In reality what happens, is that you're mostly guessing what the layer is by looking at the “tail” of its definition.
While usually, *just* seeing the name would suffice for debugging purposes.

The new `log-layer-changes-name-only` does what it sounds like it does: when `log-layer-changes` is enabled, instead of printing the entire layer definition, only the layer **name** is printed. \
By default it's disabled: the new behavior is opt-in.

I decided to not make a flag for this option, because realistically you either always want this cleaner & smaller output, or you always don't. As opposed to the `--log-layer-changes` flag, where you might use it sometimes to debug your config, but disable it otherwise for extra performance.

I updated the documentation and tests I found that mention `log-layer-changes` / `log_layer_changes`; doesn't look like I missed anything but point me if I did 😌

Performance-wise it is free, as it's a direct field access rather than unwrapping a DynGuard of some sort; and the layer name is already collected ahead of time, this option doesn't do any extra actual work.

pullRequest.title: input: Let hosts choose how completion labels are highlighted
pullRequest.body:
## Summary

The completion menu always painted a fixed prefix of each label, starting at the first byte and lasting as long as the typed word. Hosts can now supply the byte ranges to paint. Contiguous and character-by-character matchers are included, and the Editor story's Options menu shows both.

## Public API

### gpui-base

Re-exported from `gpui-component` through `input`.

- `pub type CompletionHighlighter = dyn Fn(&str, &CompletionItem) -> Vec<Range<usize>>` — byte ranges of a completion label to paint as the match.
- `pub fn highlight_prefix(query: &str, item: &CompletionItem) -> Vec<Range<usize>>` — paints a prefix of the label, using `filter_text`'s length when the item sets one.
- `pub fn highlight_contains(query: &str, item: &CompletionItem) -> Vec<Range<usize>>` — paints the first case-insensitive contiguous occurrence of the query.
- `pub fn highlight_characters(query: &str, item: &CompletionItem) -> Vec<Range<usize>>` — paints each query character in order, allowing gaps, and merges adjacent hits.
- `pub fn Lsp::with_completion_highlighter(self, highlighter: Rc<CompletionHighlighter>) -> Self` — configure label highlighting during construction.
- `pub fn Lsp::completion_highlighter(&self) -> &Rc<CompletionHighlighter>` — read the current label highlighter; defaults to `highlight_prefix`.
- `pub fn Lsp::set_completion_highlighter(&mut self, highlighter: Rc<CompletionHighlighter>)` — replace the highlighter through `lsp_mut()` and notify the editor to repaint an open menu.

## Test plan

- [x] Review fixes: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check`
- [x] Review fixes: `cargo build -p gpui-component-story`
- [x] Review fixes: `cargo test -p gpui-base --lib lsp::` (11 passed)
- [x] Launch the Editor story for manual validation

- [x] `cargo test -p gpui-base --lib completions::tests`
- [x] `cargo test -p gpui-base --doc CompletionMenuOptions`
- [x] `cargo test -p gpui-component --lib highlight_ranges_are_ordered`
- [x] In the Editor story, open Completions and type `fl` and `log`
- [x] Switch Options → Completion highlight between Prefix, Contains, and Characters, including while the menu is open
- [x] Confirm Prefix keeps only labels that start with the query, Contains keeps a contiguous hit, and Characters keeps an in-order match with gaps

Completion rows use rem-relative heights so their geometry scales with the theme base font. The highlighter is private and accessed through configuration methods.

pullRequest.title: uniffi_bindgen: apply renames through Box<T> fields
pullRequest.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3006.

`[bindings.<language>.rename]` renames a type's own definition but was leaving any field that
reaches it through `Box<T>` or `Option<Box<T>>` pointing at the old, now-renamed-away name.

Both code paths responsible for renaming skipped `Type::Box`:

- `uniffi_meta::Type::rename_recursive` (used for the Swift and Kotlin bindings) recursed into
  `Optional`, `Sequence`, `Set` and `Map`, but not `Box`.
- `uniffi_bindgen`'s general-pipeline `map_type` (used for the Python bindings) did the same,
  falling through to its `_ => ty` catch-all for `Box`.

In practice this means:
- Swift and Kotlin bindings fail to compile (the field type references a class name that no
  longer exists after the rename).
- Python bindings raise a `NameError` on import (the field's type annotation references an
  undefined name).

## Fix

Add the missing `Type::Box { inner_type }` arm to both functions, matching the existing
`Optional`/`Sequence`/`Set` handling (recurse into `inner_type`, leave everything else alone).

## Testing

- Added unit tests for `Type::rename_recursive` (`uniffi_meta/src/types.rs`) covering a plain
  `Box<T>` field and a nested `Option<Box<T>>` field.
- Added unit tests for `map_type` (`uniffi_bindgen/src/pipeline/general/types.rs`) covering the
  same two shapes, confirming the renamed name propagates while `orig_name` (the original Rust
  name) is left untouched.
- Extended `uniffi_bindgen/src/interface/rename.rs`'s existing rename test suite with a new
  `test_rename_through_box_field` test that builds a `ComponentInterface` with a `Holder` record
  containing `boxed: Box<Leaf>` and `opt_boxed: Option<Box<Leaf>>` fields, applies a
  `[bindings.*.rename]`-style rename, and asserts both fields now carry the renamed type — this
  exercises the same `ComponentInterface::visit_mut` path the real Swift/Kotlin renaming uses.
- `cargo test -p uniffi_meta -p uniffi_bindgen --lib`: all tests pass (103 total, including the 5
  new ones).
- `cargo fmt -p uniffi_meta -p uniffi_bindgen -- --check` and
  `cargo clippy -p uniffi_meta -p uniffi_bindgen --lib --tests`: clean.

### Manual verification (end to end, matching the issue's own repro)

Built the exact `Holder { plain: Leaf, boxed: Box<Leaf>, opt_boxed: Option<Box<Leaf>> }` crate from
the issue (with `[bindings.python.rename] Leaf = "PyLeaf"`, `[bindings.swift.rename] Leaf =
"SwLeaf"`, `[bindings.kotlin.rename] Leaf = "KtLeaf"`) against a local build of this branch's
`uniffi-bindgen`, and generated Python, Swift and Kotlin bindings:

- **Before the fix** (verified against the unpatched tree as a negative control): generated Swift
  has `public var boxed: Leaf` / `public var optBoxed: Leaf?` (undeclared type — would not
  compile), and generated Python has `boxed:Leaf, opt_boxed:typing.Optional[Leaf]` (undefined
  name).
- **After the fix**: Swift has `public var boxed: SwLeaf` / `optBoxed: SwLeaf?`, Kotlin has
  `var boxed: KtLeaf` / `var optBoxed: KtLeaf?`, and Python has
  `boxed:PyLeaf, opt_boxed:typing.Optional[PyLeaf]` — matching `plain`'s renamed type in all
  three.
- Actually imported and ran the generated Python module (no `swiftc`/`kotlinc` available in this
  environment, so Swift/Kotlin were checked by inspecting the generated source, not compiled):
  ```
  >>> h = m.make_holder()
  >>> h
  Holder(plain=PyLeaf(v=1), boxed=PyLeaf(v=2), opt_boxed=PyLeaf(v=3))
  >>> typing.get_type_hints(m.Holder.__init__)
  {'plain': <class 'rename_box.PyLeaf'>, 'boxed': <class 'rename_box.PyLeaf'>,
   'opt_boxed': typing.Optional[rename_box.PyLeaf]}
  ```

## Notes for reviewers

This PR (and the code fix) was written with the assistance of Claude Code, based on a manual
read of the two buggy functions and a from-scratch reproduction of the bug described in #3006 (a
fresh crate + `uniffi.toml`, built and run against both the patched and unpatched tree). I've
reviewed the diff and the verification output above myself before opening this PR.

pullRequest.title: fix(iroh): bound pending_open_paths while a connection is stuck
pullRequest.body:
## Description

Fixes #4390.

While a connection stays in `RemoteCidsExhausted` / `MaxPathIdReached`, the `None` branch of `open_path_ensure` is reached again every time `scheduled_open_path` fires (333 ms) for every candidate 4-tuple, and each pass re-pushes the same entries into `pending_open_paths`. Nothing dedups or bounds it, so the `VecDeque` grows for as long as the condition lasts.

The number of distinct candidate 4-tuples for a remote is small (single digits), so a containment check is a short linear scan and bounds the queue to that set:

```rust
if !self.pending_open_paths.contains(open_4tuple) {
    self.pending_open_paths.push_back(open_4tuple.clone());
}
```

## Notes

- We have run this patch on a small production mesh for several weeks. It removes this particular unbounded growth.
- Draft per CONTRIBUTING — happy to change the shape. If you would rather bound it by capacity, or skip the scheduling entirely when the tuple is already queued, say which you prefer and I will rework it.
- There is separate, residual memory growth we still see with this patch applied, reported in #4549; this PR is only the bounded-queue part.

## Change checklist

- [x] Self-review.
- [x] Documentation updates following the [style guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/1574-more-api-documentation-conventions.html#appendix-a-full-conventions-text), if relevant.
- [ ] Tests if relevant.
- [x] All breaking changes documented.

## Breaking Changes

None.

pullRequest.title: StreamableParser: Use replacement character for invalid utf-8 sequences
pullRequest.body:
Before, when parsing message content, if we came across any invalid utf-8 sequences, we'd forever accumulate them in `undecoded_tokens` and any subsequent content would get dropped when we eventually found our next stop token.

Now, we detect invalid utf-8 sequences and replace them with the utf-8 replacement character '\uFFFD' and continue parsing further content. In real-world scenarios, sometimes invalid utf-8 sequences are being generated by gpt-oss models. This could be caused by too high temperature settings, prompts with extensive usage of utf-8 characters in unexpected ways that are outside the training datasets, or some combination of both.

The net effect is that parsing will continue making forward progress after we hit an invalid utf-8 sequence, which is important for scenarios where inference servers are generating streaming long message contents and the users will expect those tokens to be streamed back as they're generated instead of buffered for long periods of time in our `StreamableParser`.

See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26480 for one such real-world scenario encountered in vLLM.

pullRequest.title: LWLocks for dynamic shared memory, with an ad-hoc implementation for parallel foreign scans
pullRequest.body:
The primary goal of this PR is to implement a mechanism for locking dynamic shared memory (DSM) provided to worker processes during a parallel foreign scan.

The proposed solution is based on three layers:
* a low level Rust wrapper over PostgreSQL LWLock, not tied to SHMEM hooks;
* a mechanism for requesting a LWLock tranche on startup, stored as a static global, based on the existing `PgSharedMemoryInitialization` trait and the `pg_shmem_init!` macro;
* high level components that are designed to be straightforwardly used in PostgreSQL FDW routines (`pgrx_*_foreign_scan`).

### Tests

This PR implements the same test coverage of PgLwLock for the new lock mechanisms. I didn't find a clean way to test BgWorkers and shared memory using the introduced lock types. Instead, I provided an example implementation in `pgrx-examples/parallel_scan_lwlock` that allows executing parallel scans, whose workers access a shared resource (a naive counter) as the source of tuples for foreign tables.

If you have any suggestion, I'll proceed to integrate the test suite.

pullRequest.title: fix: don't grant pg_monitor SELECT on queue/archive tables (#594)
pullRequest.body:
## Problem

Fixes #594. Since the `pg_monitor` grants were added, installing pgmq runs:

```sql
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA pgmq TO pg_monitor;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA pgmq TO pg_monitor;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA pgmq GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO pg_monitor;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA pgmq GRANT SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO pg_monitor;
```

That gives every `pg_monitor` member read access to **all** queue and archive tables,
i.e. full message payloads and headers. `pg_monitor` is meant for monitoring views and
functions, not application data, so this is an unintended data exposure. Monitoring only
needs whole-queue aggregates (`pgmq.metrics` / `pgmq.metrics_all`) and the queue list.

## Fix: column-level grants (no SECURITY DEFINER)

As suggested by @ChuckHend on the issue, `pg_monitor` is granted only the minimum the
monitoring functions read:

- `USAGE` on schema `pgmq` and `SELECT` on `pgmq.meta` (for `list_queues` / `metrics_all`) — unchanged.
- **Column-level** `SELECT (vt, enqueued_at)` on each queue table — the only columns
  `metrics()` / `metrics_all()` read (`count(*)`, `count(... vt <= now())`,
  `min/max(enqueued_at)`). `count(*)` is satisfied by column-level SELECT.
- `SELECT` on each queue's `_msg_id_seq` (for `total_messages`).

`message` / `headers` and the archive (`a_*`) tables are never granted to `pg_monitor`.
`metrics()` is unchanged from upstream (`SECURITY INVOKER`); there is **no SECURITY DEFINER
code** in pgmq. Grants are applied in `create_non_partitioned`, `create_unlogged` and
`create_partitioned` via `EXECUTE FORMAT('... ON pgmq.%I ...')` (identifier-safe). For
partitioned queues the grant on the parent is sufficient — metrics query the parent and the
privilege check happens there.

> Note: an earlier draft of this PR used a `SECURITY DEFINER` metrics function; it was
> dropped because a queue-creating role could plant a view/type/RLS policy that the definer
> would execute with the owner's privileges (privilege escalation). Column grants avoid that
> class of problem entirely.

## Upgrade path

`sql/pgmq--1.13.0--1.13.1.sql` (the unreleased version) now, in addition to the notify fix:

1. Removes the schema default privileges that granted `SELECT` to `pg_monitor` (for every
   grantor role).
2. Revokes the old broad `SELECT` from `pg_monitor` on every relation in `pgmq` except
   `meta` — queue/archive tables, partitioned parents and pg_partman children, sequences,
   and any user-added views/matviews/foreign tables over them.
3. `CREATE OR REPLACE`s the three queue-creation functions so queues created after the
   upgrade also get the column grants.
4. Backfills the column-level `SELECT (vt, enqueued_at)` + sequence `SELECT` for every
   existing queue in `pgmq.meta`.
5. Warns (never fails) if a whole-table `SELECT` for `pg_monitor` remains — e.g. a grant
   made `WITH GRANT OPTION` by a role the upgrade cannot act as, which `REVOKE` silently
   skips.

The migration is idempotent and fail-open: if the upgrading role cannot revoke/grant on an
object (not its owner), it emits a `WARNING` with the exact statement to run manually rather
than aborting `ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE`.

## pg_dump parity

The maintainer noted fresh-install vs. upgraded users could end up with different `pg_dump`
output. Because both paths now apply the **same** explicit per-queue column/sequence grants
(and neither creates schema default ACLs), a fresh install and an upgraded install produce
identical `pgmq` ACLs. Verified: `pg_dump -n pgmq --schema-only` of a fresh 1.13.1 install
and a 1.13.0→1.13.1 upgrade (same queues) are byte-identical except for pg18's random
`\restrict`/`\unrestrict` dump tokens.

Residual note: parity holds when the grantor role is the same. If pre-existing queues were
owned by different roles, the recorded grantor in each ACL entry can differ between installs;
this is inherent to per-object grants and does not change the effective privileges.

## Behavior change for operators

This is an intentional, security-relevant behavior change: after installing/upgrading,
`pg_monitor` members can no longer `SELECT` from queue or archive tables (or their
`message` / `headers` columns). Anything that relied on `pg_monitor` to read queue rows
directly will now get `permission denied` and should use `pgmq.metrics()` /
`pgmq.metrics_all()` / `pgmq.list_queues()` instead, or be granted access explicitly.

## Metrics still work

Verified on PostgreSQL 18.4 and 14.23: a `pg_monitor` member can run `pgmq.metrics()`,
`pgmq.metrics_all()` and `pgmq.list_queues()`, and can read `vt` / `enqueued_at` and the
sequence, while `SELECT * / message FROM pgmq.q_*`, `SELECT * FROM pgmq.a_*`, and
`pgmq.read(...)` are all denied with `permission denied`.

## Tests

`test/sql/base.sql` (+ `expected/base.out`) now assert, for a `pg_monitor` member:
`metrics` / `metrics_all` / `list_queues` succeed and `vt,enqueued_at` + the sequence are
readable, while the whole queue table, the `message` column, the archive table and `read()`
are denied; a role that is neither `pg_monitor` nor able to read the queue table is denied
`metrics`; the fresh install creates no `pg_default_acl` for the schema; and there is no
`SECURITY DEFINER` function in schema `pgmq`.

`make installcheck` (regression: base, fifo_per_group, fifo_rr, fifo, topic; isolation:
transaction_tests) passes on PostgreSQL 18.4. The upgrade was additionally validated by a
real `ALTER EXTENSION pgmq UPDATE '1.13.0' -> '1.13.1'` (old broad access before, denied
after; new post-upgrade queues get the column grants) and by re-running the migration for
idempotency.

pullRequest.title: opt(polars-plan): add constant folding for integer bitwise operations and NOT
pullRequest.body:
## Overview
This PR extends the expression optimizer's constant folding capabilities to support bitwise operations on integer literals and typed integer scalars. Previously, bitwise expression folding (`And`, `Or`, `Xor`, and unary `Not`) was restricted strictly to boolean literals.

## Changes Implemented
* **Integer Bitwise Evaluation (`mod.rs`)**:
  * Introduced the `eval_binary_integer_same_type!` macro to safely evaluate binary bitwise operators (`&`, `|`, `^`) across all signed (`i8` through `i128`) and unsigned (`u8` through `u128`) integer types.
  * Supports both dynamic integer literals and strictly typed scalar literals, preserving supertype coercion semantics and literal dtypes.
  * Preserves safe fallbacks (returning `None` and deferring to runtime engine execution) if types mismatch, contain nulls, or involve floats.
* **Unary NOT Folding (`simplify_functions.rs`)**:
  * Updated `IRBooleanFunction::Not` to support folding integer literals alongside booleans while strictly preserving materialized bit-widths and dtypes.
* **Testing (`test_bitwise.py`)**:
  * Added comprehensive unit test coverage in Python (`py-polars/tests/unit/operations/test_bitwise.py`) covering dynamic integer literals, typed integer scalars across various bit-widths, IR node generation, coercion semantics, and end-to-end `.collect()` execution accuracy.

pullRequest.title: refactor(core): type the activation errors
pullRequest.body:
refactor(core): type the activation errors

First `pixi_core` slice of #6707. Activation is done first because
`pixi_task` only depends on `pixi_core` through
`get_activated_environment_variables`, so it can follow right after.

All four activation entry points share one `ActivationError` enum, as
they share their failure modes. The `miette!(format!(..))` calls that
flattened rattler's error into one string become variants with a
`#[source]`, so the cause chain is kept. A panic in the blocking
activation task is now re-raised instead of turned into an error,
matching the other `spawn_blocking` sites. A failed cache write still
aborts activation, as before.

Messages follow the Rust convention of lowercase without a trailing
full stop. A failing activation script no longer prints its stdout and
the generated script: the stdout is rattler's dump of the whole
environment, which could leak secrets into logs. The script's stderr is
shown as help instead.

Message differences:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Activator creation fails | `failed to create activator for Default` + rattler message on the next line | `failed to create activator for 'default'`, rattler message as the cause |
| Same, from `pixi shell-hook` | rattler message only | `failed to create activator for 'default'`, rattler message as the cause |
| Other activation failure | `An activation error occurred: IoError(Os { .. })` | `failed to activate 'default'`, `No such file or directory (os error 2)` as the cause |
| Activation script fails | `Failed to run activation script for Default. Status: exit status: 3. Stdout: <environment dump>. Stderr: <stderr>. Script: <script>` | `failed to run activation script for 'default' (exit status: 3)`, stderr as help |
| `clean-env` on Windows | ``Currently it's not possible to run a `clean-env` option on Windows.`` | `` `clean-env` is not supported on Windows `` |
| Activation cache write fails | the io error | `failed to write the activation cache`, io error as the cause |

pullRequest.title: VM: Support Custom Syntax
pullRequest.body:
# Introduction

Custom syntax is a unique feature of Rhai, one used by many domain-specific applications to simplify code by providing new syntax suited to the domain usage.

# Grain Support
Previously, Grain rejects all custom syntax as fragments.  This PR adds support for custom syntax that does not touch the `scope`.

Custom syntax that touches the `scope`, like `eval`, remain non-lowerable. These cases are extremely rare.

# Implementation

Grain implements custom syntax via a new Opcode `Op::CustomSyntax` and a `custom_syntax` pool.

# `no_ast`

Finally, `no_ast` works with custom syntax, disabling only the parser half of it, but allows the execution part to work with Grain.

pullRequest.title: fix(gmm): use log-sum-exp in estimate_log_prob_resp to prevent overflow
pullRequest.body:
Fixes #442

## Problem

`estimate_log_prob_resp` computed the per-sample log-normaliser as:

    ln(Σ exp(xᵢ))

For tight Gaussians (small covariance, observation near the mean) the weighted
log-probabilities xᵢ can exceed ~709, causing `f64::exp()` to overflow to `inf`.
The subsequent `ln(inf)` produces an infinite `log_prob_norm`, and every `log_resp`
becomes `-inf`, collapsing all responsibilities to NaN / zero and destabilising EM.

## Fix

Replace with the **log-sum-exp trick**:

    max + ln(Σ exp(xᵢ − max))

where `max = max_i(xᵢ)` is computed independently per sample row via
`map_axis(Axis(1), ...)`. After the shift the largest exponent is 0, so
`exp()` never exceeds 1.

**Proof of equivalence:**

    max + ln(Σ exp(xᵢ − max))
    = max + ln(Σ exp(xᵢ) · exp(−max))     [exp(a−b) = exp(a)·exp(−b)]
    = max + ln(exp(−max) · Σ exp(xᵢ))     [factor out constant exp(−max)]
    = max + ln(exp(−max)) + ln(Σ exp(xᵢ)) [ln(a·b) = ln(a)+ln(b)]
    = max + (−max) + ln(Σ exp(xᵢ))        [ln(exp(−max)) = −max]
    = ln(Σ exp(xᵢ))                        ∎

Both the old and new code operate per-row (`Axis(1)`); only the intermediate
numerical range changes.

## Regression test

`test_large_weighted_log_prob_numerical_stability` builds a 70-feature,
1-component GMM with covariance `1e-10 · I`. A point at the cluster mean
produces a log-Gaussian probability of ~741 — above the f64 overflow
threshold of ~709.78. The test asserts `log_prob_norm` is finite and
responsibilities sum to 1.

pullRequest.title: Report invalid UTF-8 at the first bad byte
pullRequest.body:
When `from_utf8` failed while parsing a string, the error used the reader's current position, which is already past the closing quote. The column therefore always pointed at the end of the string, not at the invalid byte.

This uses `Utf8Error::valid_up_to` so `InvalidUnicodeCodePoint` reports the first bad byte, the same way control-character errors already do.

pullRequest.title: Impl From/TryFrom for message components
pullRequest.body:
This PR implements the From/TryFrom traits for all message components lacking the implementation.

Currently, working with existing CV2 messages (editing, etc.) can be quite painful since the conversion from each `Component` to its builder must be done manually. This makes the process much easier.

In accordance with the [std documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.From.html), I only implemented `From` for lossless conversions. Furthermore, while `SectionComponent` and `SectionAccessory` would currently be lossless conversions, I chose to impl `TryFrom` instead since the [Discord docs](https://docs.discord.com/developers/components/reference#section-section-structure) note that these types should not be hardcoded to contain only the currently available components.

Impls have not been added for modal components as I couldn't think of a valid use case and the conversions would be extremely lossy.

The PR also amends an outdated doc comment for `CreateInputText`.

pullRequest.title: fix: escape control characters in argument error messages
pullRequest.body:
When a command-line argument is invalid, fd wrote the argument into the error message and printed it without escaping control characters and a crafted argument could run terminal escape sequences.

Example: a script runs fd "$INPUT" with an untrusted pattern. An invalid regex or glob holding an escape sequence is echoed in the error, and the terminal executes it.

pullRequest.title: Add minimal pastebin behaviour
pullRequest.body: Fixes https://github.com/svenstaro/miniserve/issues/1475 My usage for this is wanting to share text between systems on an authenticated network, any more complicated "password protection", "secret" or "expiry" behaviour seen on other pastebins is out of scope. Protecting the "pastebin" can be done by existing methods in `miniserve` if desired. Viewing pastes is done by viewing the file in browser. I think that's inline with miniserves objectives, _"For when you really just want to serve some ~~files~~ text content over HTTP right now! "_. The PR allows users to create plaintext 'pastes' from the webui. The interface can be enabled with the `--pastebin` cli argument and also requires `--file-uploads` to be enabled. A textarea (required) input & title input (optional) are presented to the user. When the paste form is submitted, we create a plaintext file in memory and pass it to the exiting upload form. This means the pastebin behaviour inherits all behaviours associated with uploading files (eg: filename collisions). If no title is given we generate a `paste-{random-6-ch}.txt` filename, otherwise the given title is suffixed with `.txt`, if required, and used as the filename. This is a WIP/POC to see if the idea is acceptable, things not addressed: - [x] mobile theming (its "ok") - any theming really, all css is inline. - [ ] 'short option' name (`-P` was already taken) - [x] ctrl-enter should submit the form (common on the web). - [ ] potential notification of the name of a paste that was created? - I think you could actually skip this if no existing infra exists, and just rely on users giving their pastes a name if needed, otherwise they can sort by last-modified. - alternatively, support a fragment in the URL to highlight a file in the listing and just set that somehow on the return from uploading.

pullRequest.title: fix(plugin): preserve reconnected sidecar sessions
pullRequest.body:
## Cause
Web reconnect detached and closed the old plugin pool in the background. A late `connection/disconnect` could remove the sidecar registration created by the new `connection/connect` for the same connection ID. File and SSH operations then reported no active connection even though the Web UI had connected successfully.

## Change
- Retire the old Web plugin pool without sending a disconnect before reconnecting, matching the desktop path.
- Serialize plugin connect/disconnect calls for each connection and ignore disconnects from obsolete handles. This also covers in-flight detached closes from other paths.
- Add a mock sidecar regression test for two connects, a late old-handle disconnect, and a final explicit disconnect.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p dbx-web plugin_reconnect_ignores_late_disconnect_from_old_pool -- --nocapture` (passed on macOS)
- Targeted `rustfmt --check` and `git diff --check` (passed)

pullRequest.title: nrf52: Remove `unsafe` `StaticRef` constructors from individual peripherals
pullRequest.body:
### Pull Request Overview

This is part of my quest to move the nrf52 crate to be mostly safe, and only have the necessary unsafe code in dedicated unsafe crates. In this part of the series, this moves all† of the of the `StaticRef` constructors to chip.rs. This removes the unsafe code from the actual driver, setting the driver to be in a safe crate.

For many peripherals, this is straightforward: move the static ref to chip.rs, add the register static ref as an argument to new(), update default peripherals.

For some, this is a lot more involved. Things like UICR, APProtect, and FICR are used in various places in board files. I updated these to use the same format as any other peripheral. Also, UICR and APProtect use FICR, so that is now constructed in the board and passed in so a reference can be given to uicr and approtect.

Peripherals like USB and 15.4 radio are only used in specific variants, and so this moves those static refs to those chips.




† I didn't move uart because that is being changed in a different PR.

This is but a step on a long journey. By doing this step in its own PR, the change to reorg crates into safe/unsafe will be much smaller and easier to reason about.

pullRequest.title: Add wasm32-unknown-emscripten target support
pullRequest.body:
Resolves #642.

Adds `wasm32-unknown-emscripten` as a target for mio, with a CI job running the suite under Node. Opening as a draft for now since it depends on unreleased patchsets for Emscripten and Rust's libc.

This lays the groundwork for Tokio support for Emscripten. Initially I did not plan to PR Mio, but in discussion with @Darksonn and @Noah-Kennedy it was suggested to use Mio if possible, and this has worked out well in my opinion.

With https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/pull/27207 landed, Emscripten now exposes a real epoll, so the existing Linux epoll selector can reused rather than adding a new backend.

### Patch Sets

This PR required the following upstream patches, now all merged:

- [x] https://github.com/rust-lang/socket2/pull/660 - Socket2 Emscripten support (landed, pending release)
- [x] emscripten-core/emscripten#27207 — The epoll APIs for Emscripten
- [x] https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/pull/5427 libc epoll definitions in libc@0.2.190 release
- [x] emscripten-core/emscripten#27306 — NODERAWSOCKETS: socket fstat and SO_TYPE/SO_LINGER/TCP_MAXSEG options
- [x] rust-lang/libc#5256 — emscripten: add in6_pktinfo struct (merged)
- [x] Rust nightly patches in stable

### Test status

The tests run under `-pthread -sPROXY_TO_PTHREAD` in Emscripten.

In order to support the blocking accept, it was necessary to refactor the test suite to support non-blocking sockets via a `util::accept` / `util::read` abstraction.

Tests run directly on the Emscripten Node.js build with `NODERAWSOCKETS` and `NODERAWFS` to provide a transparent runner without further harness configuration being necessary.

* 147 passed, 0 failed
* 3 ignored: `tcp_stream::raw_fd` (Emscripten `getsockname` reports `0.0.0.0` as the local address until a non-blocking connect completes; port is stable since emscripten-core/emscripten#27566, address fix pending).
