pullRequest.title: Show "group not found" messages on Linux
pullRequest.body:
Previously, if an incorrect group was specified using a command like `./target/release/sudo -u#1 -g#555 id`, the user was shown the following error message on some Ubuntu Linux installations

```
sudo: IO error: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

This occurred because we were only showing the existing group not found message when the `getgrgid_r()` and `getgrnam_r()` functions returned 0. However, per the docs, the functions can also return ENOENT, ESRCH, EBADF, or EPERM, among others.

This patch adds the other documented failure return values to the "return 0" case so that sudo-rs returns a more informative error message on some Ubuntu Linux installs when a group is not found.

pullRequest.title: Refactor database importer to be channel-based
pullRequest.body:
## Product change and motivation

  Database import now streams items from the gRPC import service to a dedicated importer task through a bounded queue, instead of running each request as a blocking step inside the service. This prepares the importer for parallel writers, and fixes several problems with how imports stop, fail and are reported:
  
  - **Shutdown and close no longer wait on an import.** Server shutdown, import close and client disconnect are noticed while the service is waiting on the importer (a full queue or a long finalisation), and the import is aborted.
  - **Shutdown is clean.** The importer runs as a task tracked by the server's background task tracker, so shutdown waits for it to stop and release the staged database, even if its handle was dropped without being aborted.
  - **Importer failures are reported immediately**, with the importer's actual error, instead of against the client's next request.
  - **Staged databases are cleaned up on every failure and stop path**, including a failed finalisation. An import that completes while being stopped is kept and reported as done.
  - **A client that stops sending mid-import adds why.** If the request stream ends or errors while an import is active, the import is discarded and the client receives a `ClientClosed` error, instead of the response stream just ending.
  - **A `ReqPart` or `Done` before `InitialReq` returns an error** (`ImportNotInitialised`) instead of panicking the service task.
  - **The reported item count** no longer includes deferred ownerships and role players written during finalisation.

  Note that this change disables the periodic progress log of imported item counts: submitting an item to the queue doesn't mean it has been processed. The final count is still logged when an import completes.

  ## Implementation

  - **`DatabaseImporterHandle`:** `DatabaseImporter::start` creates the queue and the interrupt, spawns the importer as a blocking task via the new `TokioTaskSpawner::spawn_blocking`, and returns this handle. 
    - The handle is the only way to send the importer items. Dropping it aborts the import.
    - Items are decoded on the importer task: for now, by passing an iterator that performs the conversion.
  - **`DatabaseImportService`:** keeps an `ActiveImport` holding the handle, instead of running importer steps itself.
    - `StopSignals` races waits on the importer against shutdown, close and client disconnect.
    - The service loop also watches the importer's result, so failures are reported and cleaned up immediately.
    - Stream end, a gRPC error and every failure all go through one close path, which aborts and discards an unfinished import and reports the reason to the client.
  - **Diagnostics:** `DatabasesImport` is recorded once per import, with its final outcome.
  - **Naming:** `DatabaseImportHandler` is now `ImportingDatabaseHandle`

pullRequest.title: Support the sink symbol _ in place of vector operands
pullRequest.body:
PTX allows `_` as a sink in place of a vector operand, e.g. `mov.b64 {_, %r1}, %rd1;` or `ld.global.v4.u32 {_, %r2, _, _}, [%rd1];`. The lexer rejected a lone `_` with a TokenError, which fails the whole module; CuPy's cuRAND PTX uses it heavily.

- The lexer accepts `_` as an identifier.
- When `_` is a destination, identifier resolution declares a fresh register of the operand's type in its place.
- Vector unpack elements get their element type (a `.b64` split in two gives `.b32`).

`_` as a source element (e.g. in a `.v8` store) is still unsupported. Adds `test_ptx!(sink, ...)` (`sink.ptx`, `ll/sink.ll`).

PTX reference, section 9.2: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.1/pdf/ptx_isa_9.4.pdf

> For some instructions the destination operand is optional. A bit bucket operand denoted with an un
derscore (_) may be used in place of a destination register.

pullRequest.title: Refactor vulkano-shaders
pullRequest.body:
I just wanted to implement the `entry_point` macro option, but the amount of cruft that vulkano-shaders has built up over the years is so bad that it's neigh impossible to make a change at this point, so here I am refactoring almost everything.

Here are some highlights:
- Use of empty strings as sentinel values. The worst of this was the hash map, where an empty string key meant that that's the only entry. Since what's being represented is either just one value or a map of key-value pairs, the ideal solution is an enum of precisely those two.
- Other data that wasn't represented well, like `SourceKind`, and `MacroInput` not being split into two.
- State being stored in many different stack variables, making it very hard to split things into smaller functions.
- Functions being too big to understand.
- Functions being split into functions where they shouldn't have been.
- Code duplication.
- Inconsistency.

Apart from that, I also made the diagnostics a bit more helpful and consistent, and improved the docs. In particular, the code in the headings made links to those headings really bad, making linking to other parts of the same docs unpleasant. Also, the new docs have more room to properly show the syntax of each option.

I suggest reviewing one commit at a time.

Fixes #2822

Changelog:
```markdown
### Additions
- Vulkano-shaders: Added a `compiler` macro option, which allows you to specify the shader compiler to use.
- Vulkano-shaders: Added an `entry_point` macro option, which allows you to specify the entry point of the shader source to compile.
```
